Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_2_01_06: 26 years, that's how long it'll take me to work off my debt.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_S_07_01_04: <metal creaks> God damn it. I can't take this.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_S_10_01_07: A clean base has meaning. Go get rid of the cysts, you heroic pioneer. Maybe then the IRO bigwigs will give you a 5-minute break.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_4_02_08: Aaaaah! Oh fuck, oh fuck, oh fuck, it hurts so much.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_7_01_08: Alright, we'll just have to subsist on fruit.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_S_10_01_08: And make sure to get them all, or they'll fine you and they'll send you to a mine for the next 150 years.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_2_01_10: And now the aliens will get you.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_4_01_05: At least 10 meters! He fell down to the bottom!
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_7_01_06: At least we don't have to worry about True Death.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_S_15_01_02: Bart, come in! I need you, Bart! They got me, I can't…
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_S_07_01_03: But now that I've heard it, it's all I hear. It feels like my brain is creaking. I can't sleep, I can't calm down, all I hear is creak, creak, creak.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_S_10_01_04: But thanks to us, Selenian will get rich on its government contract and will be able to make more factories to provide jobs to all those people
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_7_01_05: But we did get double the biofilament.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_2_01_09: Carlos! He's a wanted criminal, if I hadn't said anything they would've gotten me too!
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_2_01_01: Carlos, you locked the door! Let me in!
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_6_01_10: Chill, what can they do to us here? We'll have one less problem to worry about.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_3_02_01: Come on, Diego, they're still far behind!
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_3_02_05: Come on, you can get this patched up.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_S_10_01_01: Did you read this shit? This fucking propaganda is killing me.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_3_02_06: Don't add on another five years for just a flesh wound.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_3_02_07: Don't stuff me into a sleeve right away… I'll rest a bit in the afterlife.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_2_01_03: Everything's exploding! They killed Patricia! Open up!
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_S_15_01_01: Fuck! How do you… Bart, you okay?
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_2_01_07: Fuck, they blew up the bio-printers, I'm gonna die here .Really die here.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_S_07_01_01: George Clarke, day 17 report. I discovered what's causing the strange test results.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_3_02_04: Go get Ben, I'll just go ahead and die here.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_3_01_01: Go see where Ben is, he's not answering his communicator.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_6_01_03: He snitched on me for reading Jax's report. I got slapped with a gigantic fine. It's the penal colony for me when I get back. He literally ruined my life.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_S_15_02_01: Help! Where are you? Mark? Say something. Write me back, please, I'm stuck. Mark. Write me.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_7_02_01: Henrik, Ximena's dead. Where's the biofilament?
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_7_02_07: Henrik? How much of that stuff did you eat? Ximena's really gonna die.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_6_01_01: Hey, keep an eye on that grunt.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_4_02_06: How… What? How could you? Behind you!
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_4_01_06: I can't hold it! Come back!
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_6_01_05: I didn't, only you and Olaf know, he must've overheard or looked through my tablet.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_4_02_03: I don't care, I'm not leaving him!
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_S_10_01_06: I don't know, it felt quite nice to read that. It's as if my life finally had meaning.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_7_02_03: I looked everywhere, there's none left.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_S_XX_01_03: I looked through all of the catalogs, there's nothing on any Zamenhof anywhere.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_3_01_03: I saw him go upstairs. I'm going. What happened?
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_7_02_02: I should have it somewhere. Wait, I’ll go get it.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_2_01_11: I'll pay you, open the door, I'm begging you.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_S_XX_01_05: It was Thomas Brooks that was supposed to be going with us. The earliest entry on Zamenhof is from the day of the launch.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_3_02_02: I… I won't… I won't make it.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_S_13_01_06: Last time you drank it you said you were running a capybara farm somewhere in the jungle.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_S_XX_01_01: Marco, do you read? I checked him. Are you there?
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_S_XX_01_09: Me too. We have to be careful.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_7_02_09: My head hurts. Hurts a lot.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_7_01_09: No way, I'm not going out there. I'm a chemist, not a scout, no one trained me.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_6_02_06: No, he's got some LEMs, he'll be fine. That'll teach him to snitch on his colleagues.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_6_01_02: Of course, the guy's got a stick up his ass.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_4_02_09: Oh god, I'm gonna be sick, hold on.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_7_01_10: Okay, I'll see what I can do.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_3_01_05: Okay, so we still have some time. Maybe we'll skip the procedures and I'll revive him myself.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_S_10_01_09: One of these days you'll get in trouble for talking like that.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_S_07_01_02: Our base is constantly creaking. Dad wrote to the company about this yesterday but there's nothing we can do. Thankfully, the creaking happens at regular intervals, so it'll be easy to filter out.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_4_01_01: Peggy! Hold on to the rope! I almost fell!
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_7_01_07: Printing sleeves still costs money so I wouldn't go crazy with it.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_3_01_06: Thanks, I'm lost when it comes to those machines.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_6_02_02: There are equipment stations in the grunt's room.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_3_01_02: They got Diego, we need a new sleeve.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_7_01_03: They sent us only 25% of the food they were supposed to.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_S_13_01_07: This is different. My stomach hurts…
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_4_01_02: This isn't easy for me, you know!
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_6_02_07: Uh, but we need him now. Olaf's not responding.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_3_01_04: Vermin got him out patrolling, he got wounded.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_7_02_04: WHAT? NONE? THERE HAS TO BE SOME!
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_6_01_06: We could do something about that. He carries the keycard to that booth of his with him.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_6_02_01: We need weapons. The station's not working.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_4_02_15: We're not getting out of here.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_4_02_17: We're not getting out, we don't have the Building Tool. It came off along with my arm.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_4_02_14: We're safe here, let's wait for them to leave. I hope Ethan makes it till then.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_6_01_08: Well, Olaf got convicted for pickpocketing, and the grunt's not very careful with his backpack.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_S_13_01_05: What's that got to do with anything?
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_7_01_04: What? How are we supposed to work here without food?
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_6_01_04: Why'd you tell him what you were reading?
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_S_10_01_03: Yeah, heroic pioneers. Working their asses off for a fraction of what the suits are making at the IRO.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_S_10_01_02: Yeah. But at least they called us heroic pioneers.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_6_02_05: You haven't let him out yet? It's been like a week.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_M_2_01_04: You're not the only one who reads other people's emails.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_S_13_01_08: You're starting to piss me off. It's like babysitting a 5-year-old.
Audiologs_contentUpdate_1.AB_S_10_01_05: who always dreamed of toiling away 20 hours a day to not be able to afford even one sleeve for the next 150 years.

Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_MachineBody_01_002: <silence on the other end or some static, individual clicks>
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_MainFrame_01_001: <w tle częściowo wytłumione dźwięki kroków, gniecionego metalu, okrzyki przerażenia>
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Corridor_02_008: According to Dr. Vaughn, those monsters are drawn to electricity
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Conference_01_022: According to the regulations that apply to you as well,
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Conference_01_011: As the leader of this mission and an IRO representative, I am well within my rights,
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Conference_01_027: I am revoking your access to a body, as your role is not considered essential to the mission.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Conference_01_019: I have a list of your emails here. You contacted a certain
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Conference_01_033: I have nothing more to add. End recording.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Conference_01_001: I'm letting you know this conversation is being recorded.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Conference_01_003: I'm letting you know this conversation is being recorded. Aiden Patel, head logistician,
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Conference_01_015: Mr. Costa, I have already warned you more than once. I also have reason to believe
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Conference_01_008: The regulations leave me no choice.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Clone_01 _001: When I agreed to take the role of head logistician of the IRO mission to the Ruptura System,
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Conference_01_031: You can file a complaint to any IRO space outpost.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_TechLab_01_004: Almost everyone has been put to sleep already.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_TechLab_01_006: And maybe one day they'll retrieve the discs, or maybe they won't.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Corridor_01_004: Are you still there? Answer me!
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_TechLab_01_007: At least the higher-ups won't have to listen to us plead for help.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_TechLab_01_014: Besides, I'd do it so that the computer could be quickly fixed again, just in case.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_MainEntrance_01_007: Blow it up! Blow it up!
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_MainEntrance_01_003: Kill it! They can't get inside!
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_MainEntrance_01_001: Who opened this? Close the entrance! Immediately!
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Corridor_02_001: Since I'm already talking to myself, I might as well record it, maybe someone will find this useful.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Corridor_02_011: They're close. I'll try to get to the lab at the other end of the hallway,
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_RoadToTechLab_01_003: Alright, I evacuated, but I left something behind and I can't go back now, there's something wrong with the capsule.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_RoadToTechLab_01_001: Peter? Peter? There's a lot of aliens here, but I'm going to get the core from the technical lab. Peter?
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_MainFrame_01_009: Ci wszyscy ludzie zginęli przeze mnie…
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_TechLab_02_004: It could help us hide from them if we ever need to.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_TechLab_02_013: It's just that it'd be good to have a plan for a worst case scenario.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Lab_01_010: There's still a chance to fix this. Let's try the method with hydrolysis, like I was saying before.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Lab_01 _003: This is only the first stage of terraforming. We need to gather more data.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Lab_01 _007: You can still fix this. We'll run additional experiments.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Corridor_01_008: Hang in there, I'm going to minus two, maybe I can turn the generator back on manually.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Corridor_02_002: How could the IRO let this happen? This mission was one of its top priority projects,
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Conference_01_006: I am unfortunately forced to fine you and suspend you from your responsibilities indefinitely.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Clone_01 _004: I believed that placing the discs inside the storeroom was the best solution.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_MainFrame_01_005: I broke the computer and I should be the one to fix it, but I can't!
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Clone_01 _002: I considered it a great opportunity and a great honor.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Clone_01 _005: I could blame the IRO, say that they didn't give me a choice…
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Clone_01_007: I could have predicted that the monsters would attack the storeroom with the discs. I could have secured it better.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_MainFrame_01_006: I damaged the core. Those monsters cut me off.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Clone_01 _003: I didn't expect the mission to end in such terrible tragedy…
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Corridor_02_006: I don't believe the IRO would leave us here to die!
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Corridor_02_003: I don't believe the government could be this incompetent…
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Corridor_02_005: I don't trust that logistician, he was always up to something behind our backs…
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Corridor_01_007: I hope your Audiocom just broke.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Clone_01_009: I take full responsibility for the deaths of those people. True deaths!
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_TechLab_02_008: I think that… they feed on it somehow.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Corridor_01_005: I tried to come as soon as I got your message, but the generator went down.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Conference_01_009: I would also prefer to be addressed formally.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_MachineBody_01_007: I'm going over there myself and you better open the door for me!
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_MainFrame_01_010: I'm sorry, I really didn't mean for this to happen! It wasn't supposed to be like this!
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Conference_01_034: I'm sorry, Luca, I had no choice.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_MainFrame_01_008: I'm sorry, there's really nothing else I can do!
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_MainFrame_01_004: I'm sorry, this is all my fault!
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_TechLab_02_002: I've noticed interesting behavior among the aliens. You should know about this.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_MainFrame_01_007: If anyone with access to the technical storeroom is listening to this, we need a new core.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_TechLab_02_015: If you really want to look into this, fine, but in your free time.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_MainFrame_01_003: It should work… This fucking computer should be working! I did everything right!
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Entrance_01_002: I bet the battery's come loose.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Entrance_01_004: It's fine, it has to be the battery.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Entrance_01_010: James Mesmer: Na pewno łatwiej przeżyć na zewnątrz. Weź ze sobą baterie gdybyśmy mieli wrócić, zabrałem te z dołu do stworzenia ładunku.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Entrance_01_012: James Mesmer: Nie ma sensu bycie zjedzonym przez te cosie. Nie ma sensu umieranie z głodu. Nie ma sensu gnicie w szafce. To ma bardzo dużo sensu.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Entrance_01_008: James Mesmer: Wiem, co robię. Znajdź kombinezon, niech wszyscy znajdą.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Conference_01_030: Aiden, you're kidding, right? Don't do this to me, come on.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Conference_01_024: And what the fuck was I supposed to do?
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_MachineBody_01_003: Can you hear me? We have no food! We're starving! We need help!
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_MachineBody_01_005: Go to hell! You think you're safe?
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Conference_01_002: Like every other conversation in this place.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_MachineBody_01_001: S.O.S. I repeat S.O.S.! This is Luca Costa, an engineer from the atmosphere adjustment project! Over!
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Conference_01_013: Stop with those regulations. I mean, okay, give me the fine,
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Conference_01_032: When and how would I do that?
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Conference_01_010: You can't suspend me, I'm not going into a drawer for god knows how long.
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_TechLab_01_003: Because I can't. The empty hallways are scaring me…
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Lab_01_008: How long will that take? Several years? Dozens? We shouldn't have sent the mission so quickly,
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_TechLab_01_016: I don't know… maybe we should talk to Aiden about this?
Audiologs_FE.FE_01_A_Lab_01 _001: I don't understand these results… According to the calculations, the atmosphere should've attained optimal composition by now,

ContentUpdate_1.007_3_D_MediumBase_c_Content:
Chapter 14 - The bizarre delicacies of the preiroid era

[…] Let's be honest. You're reading this chapter not because of the rightfully by-gone rotten eggs and pickled herring, you're all waiting for the really controversial topics. Yes, before the IRO, it would happen that people would eat... people.

I will stress right at the start that this was not a widespread practice, eating human meat was not popular in any nation's cuisine, it happened almost always in extreme situations or as part of a ritual.

In the past, people were not able to print sleeves, losing one's body resulted in the True Death of the individual, so people became irrationally attached to bodies, often seeing the meat as the person they had feelings for. This created one of the strongest moral taboos connected with eating humans. It also made sense from an evolutionary standpoint. Eating members of one's own species did not provide any advantages in the Darwinian race.

Among the dangers of eating human meat are:
- Prion diseases (including Kuru)
- Autoimmune diseases
- Viral diseases
- Social exclusion
- Severe psychological trauma
- Many others

Of course, nowadays the taboo remains, though the biological dangers could be easily circumvented. Once again, our motto applies here - history is always relevant. The biofilament we use today to create sleeves was invented at a time when cannibalism was a huge social taboo, so each of our sleeves contains patented compounds that prevent the consumption of tissue printed in the Regeneration Chambers in quantities larger than simply biting one's nails. And so we're left to enjoy delicious synthetic animal meat. [...]
ContentUpdate_1.009_1_D_SmallBase_c_Content:
Chapter 4

[…] I didn't eat my algae today on purpose, just so that I could stuff my face here. I couldn't get over the delicacies in the menu. They had real pork! My mouth filled with saliva. My hunger almost made me forget I was angry at Eduardo. I looked at my communicator. Zero messages. Over an hour late. When the irritated waiter started walking my way for the fourth time, a man sat down at my table.
- I'm sorry, this is taken - I spoke up shyly.
He looked into my eyes angrily and I immediately felt the same chills that I felt last night. I had no doubt.
- Edie? - I asked.
- Eduardo - he corrected me.
- Did you change your body?
He didn't answer, instead he waved the waiter over. I got used to his previous sleeve, I fantasized about it, but there was something intriguing about this new one. Is he going to keep changing like this every day? Every... night? I blushed just thinking about it.
- We'll take two pheasants please - he said to the waiter.
- Actually, I'd rather... - I stopped, silenced by Eduardo's glare.
- Two pheasants - he repeated. He was so manly. Is he the same in bed? [...]

ContentUpdate_1.007_2_D_MediumBase_c_Content:
From: Dr. Henrik Nystrom
To: Mantis Head base personnel

It worked! It looks like I was able to clean the biofilament. This means we're not condemned to wander the dangerous surface of Arcadia. Everyone's invited over for dinner. Courtesy of Future Health Solutions and their delivery department.

Don't spread this information around. Officially, we managed to survive on fruit. I don't even want to know what fine they'd slap us with for this.
ContentUpdate_1.007_1_D_MediumBase_c_Content:
From: Future Health Solutions
To: Dr. Henrik Nystrom

Dr. Nystrom,

We did notice a mistake in the transport. However, we are unable to provide a food shipment at this time. We will notify you of a possible date in a future email.

But there's a silver lining! Since you received an excess of biofilament, we recommend printing out a new sleeve in our reliable Regeneration Chamber if you are nearing death from starvation!

Please also remember that our company's Food Stations are perfectly capable of processing all kinds of edible intermediary goods. All you have to do is put in a piece of fruit, press a button, and you will immediately receive a full-fledged meal, full of nutrients!

Persevere!
Future Health Solutions — For modern problems
ContentUpdate_1.004_1_D_MediumBase_c_Content:
From: Moon Energy Corporation
To: Ethan Jackson

Hello,

We are not happy with how you are conducting the mission. Current power usage is only at 87% of the expected amount. If you do not increase it to at least 97% in the next eight Earth days we will be forced to treat this as deliberate sabotage.

You will then be retired and replaced with another willing individual, while Dr. Peggy Chen will assume command. You will, of course, be punished accordingly.

Best Regards,
The Moon Energy Corporation


—


From: Ethan Jackson
To: Moon Energy Corporation

I assure you this is not the result of sabotage. The efficiency of the photovoltaic cells is simply not as high as the calculations would suggest. I suspect this is due to the differences in the atmosphere caused by Ruptura's unstable behavior. Our team will do what it can, but I can't make any promises. I understand the need for haste, but please increase the deadline to at least fourteen Earth days.

Respectfully,
Dr. Ethan Jackson


—


From: Moon Energy Corporation
To: Ethan Jackson


Our calculations are not wrong. Eight days.

Best Regards,
The Moon Energy Corporation HR Department
ContentUpdate_1.003_2_D_MediumBase_c_Content:
From: Selenian Corporation
To: S0214

We've registered the use of a new sleeve. As per your contract, your debt has increased by an additional 72,000 UC. Its current total is 684,300 UC.

Sincerely,
The Selenian Corporation


—


From: S0214
To: Selenian Corporation

72 thousand? So far each sleeve was only 40k. Are you out of your mind? Not to mention I died because of shoddy safeguards. That's like 5 years of work.

Convict S0214


—


From: Selenian Corporation
To: S0214

Please watch your tone. The price of sleeves has increased due to current market conditions as well as your team's excessive use of them. Ignorance of the contract does not exempt you from adhering to it.

It's too bad, you were our favorite crew.
The Selenian Corporation.

ContentUpdate_1.003_4_D_MediumBase_p_Content:
I have lived a long life. I still remember the beginnings of the IRO. I remember when we truly needed it. Hell, my parents voted for them in the first election. It made sense back then, but now… Two centuries of eating algae and shit from the Food Station. I don't remember the last time I tasted real meat, that had to be back in the 21st century. People shouldn't live that long.

Let this be my manifesto. My disc will break by the time rescue arrives. I was born in Rosario as a proud Argentinean, I die as a disgraced convict at the ass-end of space. Far from the home I can't go back to. I am not M1023, I'm Benedicto Duggan and I hereby renounce all of my debt. Fuck you all. Vete a la mierda Selenian.

Datapads_Caves.009_1_D_Cave_Content:
A0437: Where are you? Tommy?

E2138: YOU'LL NEVER FIND ME.

A0437: Don't be so dramatic. Send us your coordinates.

E2138: I'M NOT GOING BACK THERE.

A0437: What? Alright, I thought you got lost but you're just goofing off. Get back here / send us your coordinates or we'll fine you. We've got a lot of work to do.

E2138: YOU DIDN'T SEE WHAT I SAW.

A0437: Orders are orders, you can't just up and leave.

E2138: I CAN. I'M SAFE HERE.

A0437: Okay, final decision. Are you coming back or not? And stop it with the caps lock, I don't remember if there's anything about proper writing etiquette in the regulations but there's definitely something about yelling at your superior and that's what you're doing right now.

E2138: I'M NOT GOING BACK.

A0437: Fine, but the company will charge your family. Let me know if you want to come back. I'll try and delay their debt collection as long as I can.

E2138: I'M NOT GOING BACK, I WON'T LET IT GET INSIDE MY HEAD AGAIN, IT'S LIKE SCRAPING INSIDE MY BRAIN, I CAN'T GO THROUGH IT AGAIN

E1305: Okay, I'll send out a team, but we don't have a lot of time. We're going back soon.

Datapads_FE.22_D_Basement_mail_01_c_Content:
A facility cooling test has been planned for tomorrow. As you know, keeping the ideal temperature inside is key to our survival. At the same time, be informed that going through the cooling station tomorrow afternoon is forbidden!

Remember that we can't close the station completely due to security reasons and going into it during the test could not only result in damaged equipment but the potential differences in temperature could lead to damage/destruction of your sleeve and, in extreme cases, even your disc. Just make sure you don't go in there.
Datapads_FE.07_D_Lab_01_c_Content:
After conducting a series of lab tests and field trials on a limited scale, I've decided that Plan C yields the best results. Additional experiments have shown that the proposed changes in atmosphere will not have a serious effect on the local flora but will significantly increase the filtering out of cosmic radiation.

After entering the parameters of Plan C into the Engine, we began the process of changing the atmosphere. Before I discuss the results, I'd like to emphasize that the Engine works - in the sense that it affects the Planet's atmosphere. That effect, however, differs from my previous calculations.

Initial observations indicate that the atmosphere's composition does not change according to the plan. The most concerning is the increased concentration of alkanes. According to Dr. Kelsey, this allows us to generate electricity straight out of the atmosphere. I've consented to additional research being carried out in that area, at least until we're able to properly calibrate the Engine. I was worried about the effect this would have on the flora, but Dr. Santos has not observed any species dying out.

The reason for the machine not working as intended might be a calculation error. It's also possible I underestimated the strength of the chemical reactions occurring in the atmosphere because of Ruptura's effects. I certainly view the activation of the Engine as progress and I'm collecting any and all data that will help us perfect the machine. I need time to conduct another series of experiments. This could take months or even years, considering the unpredictability of Ruptura.
Datapads_FE.20_D_Alarm_black_01_c_Content:
CODE BLACK GENERATOR FAILURE IN LOGISTICS SECTOR

SWITCHING TO EMERGENCY POWER

PROTECT DISC AT ALL COSTS
Datapads_FE.04_D_Alarm_red_01_c_Content:
CODE RED EXOBIOLOGICAL BEINGS INSIDE

SECURE KEY AREAS

DO NOT LET THEM NEAR THE MAIN ENGINE
