Dialogue.02DF1EC1462966B2FDFA949F8130B147_A_G_Gri: No, they added your number at the beginning and it ends with "good luck with program Argos". That's nice of them, right?
Dialogue.E2BCA6FC4061B5F8395323BB8EE2BF6E_A_G_Gri: Yes! More rewards from the Griffits Blue Corporation are waiting to be claimed.
Dialogue.9EED0F5B4E83FFA87C350581AF09B7C8_A_G_Gri: Wow! You have fulfilled another order from the Griffits Blue Corporation! Claim your reward.
Dialogue.EF2826B34053D9DF811A4DB0550C71CD_A_G_Gri: I didn't need to simulate the sound, the meaning of the message remains the same. Drum roll. Another task for the Griffits Blue Corporation completed!
Dialogue.8CF615CE40BED402378838AE0DC51A1D_A_P_Hea: I can go back to work.
Dialogue.C36E2B104165BF3B41070BACD61FAE9D_A_E_Hun: I'm so hungry I feel sick.
Dialogue.1333A7124C83F22588348397344B138B_A_P_Idl: I don't get it, Sam, what's so interesting in beetles or flowers?
Dialogue.2A7FC9274EACBF02AC988AAB00AAEAEA_A_M_Idl: They're part of the world we live in and are inextricably connected to it. We wouldn't exist without beetles or flowers.
Dialogue.E9133C154121C0A4AC66FE8CB6BC8525_A_P_Idl: We wouldn't exist without fundamental forces! Beetles and flowers can be easily replaced with automated systems. You can't replace electromagnetism.
Dialogue.3B08F6754BAAD349F31416B0A299525B_A_M_Idl: You'd really want to live in a world without plants?
Dialogue.B7CD7ADD43383E56C2D26882271C1D9D_A_M_Idl: Chris, as an astrophysicist, you must be intrigued by how Ruptura behaves.
Dialogue.EBD74F634C31163AE6D9F0B5C882C0A4_A_P_Idl: Of course! If we understand the processes occurring inside it we will deepen our understanding of the universe!
Dialogue.63593BF341646A6E6D7E68BB2196E830_A_P_Idl: Sam, you seem to be the only scientifically competent person here. Could you look at my calculations when you have a moment? I'm designing a dome under which a city could be built.
Dialogue.964C05E84482DC090413CEAC2CFB14C7_A_M_Idl: I'm not sure that's such a good idea.
Dialogue.980D9F964821361837D94F998F4EE5BD_A_P_Idl: I am, of course, also considering tunnels like on Mars. But designing a structure that could withstand Ruptura is simply much more intellectually stimulating.
Dialogue.73DB522149B29CD7F09418B0AF5E17A8_A_M_Idl: I don't think we should be colonizing this planet at all.
Dialogue.1B585C9A4F33809DEB12E3B6617A850A_A_P_Idl: If only this wealth could reach the people in need and not corporations…
Dialogue.1658C2DB41AD7D78D95BCF97D6684DA8_A_M_Idl: Money goes to those who have earned it.
Dialogue.A4C4D63641CD573D45AD46845990C66B_A_P_Idl: Not everyone has the same opportunities like…
Dialogue.4BBBB22B40B094C7E73A70BA2FD0270D_A_M_Idl: Everyone has opportunities if they only make the effort. Stop crying over lazy slackers.
Dialogue.ABA2C52C47A9D798ED26A1AA1437181B_A_P_Idl: You don't have any patients here, you can finally focus on scientific work. No distractions, only alien organisms to focus on.
Dialogue.8747EBEF48BC582E8471CC98001065EB_A_M_Idl: To be honest, I like taking care of my patients.
Dialogue.1884A6484F4FECFB22C0CEB472D48822_A_P_Idl: I can't wait until we figure out a better way to fuel the biological body. Food is extremely inefficient.
Dialogue.7B0486C44DB8486125827BABEACF89E8_A_M_Idl: And your mind doesn't ever get tired?
Dialogue.39EF6D574B91739FE996E484DF81DB9D_A_P_Idl: Hmm… maybe when I have nothing to work on. But that almost never happens.
Dialogue.1BC9D1B14F33F0FD60636F8C4C45B2A9_A_P_Idl: Sam, I was thinking about what you said once, that you wouldn't want to live in a world without plants. Why is that?
Dialogue.9651E47D4B16F713D8B78DA3B04FE093_A_M_Idl: Because all living things are beautiful and fascinating.
Dialogue.9CFD602745CD2F25ADD1F7B6748314C9_A_P_Idl: That's it? The beauty reason? I thought you were much more rational than that.
Dialogue.B66E97814F49C1BE6C1E8688F6C7EEA6_A_M_Idl: It's not just my own personal preference. We evolved in nature. Being in nature is calming to us. It's a basic human trait.
Dialogue.0BDA759C4F91FDF5A0FC829CAD0E75D4_A_P_Idl: A trait easily forgotten. Plus we'll be able to re-program our brains in the future to get rid of defects like that. Claywood was able to copy an entire mind! It's a milestone towards thought engineering.
Dialogue.19ABDA98414B1BC0FE2E45AAEC50F21F_A_M_Idl: You want a world where people's thoughts and reactions are controlled by algorithms digging through their brains?
Dialogue.B0E1AF6B47601DC9285858853A96BDED_A_P_Idl: I want a world in which we'll finally overcome senseless atavism and reach our full potential.
Dialogue.EE3C7F54414789FACE8C3AAA76A96E30_A_P_Idl: Too slowly! There's so much to do!
Dialogue.2D2A56EC4441573B206D6E9C5C536CE6_A_M_Idl: Heh, under different circumstances this really would have been a fascinating place for researchers.
Dialogue.A6FC383145A5095BCAC323BCC235C5D8_A_P_Idl: The circumstances are perfect! We have the whole planet to ourselves!
Dialogue.389216C249FD81F3FABADC9043D6CCCB_A_M_Idl: Do you want someone to help you?
Dialogue.338334A94D45A2F2A65A5FB8EB9262C9_A_P_Idl: I prefer to work alone. Someone else might have gotten it wrong.
Dialogue.ED34B5ED486AE9050018FF8AC181FB44_A_P_Idl: Okay, Sam, what if you could move your disc into an ideal robotic body, would you do it? A hypothetical model that thinks several times faster, doesn't get tired, doesn't feel pain, can do things impossible to man.
Dialogue.A47427C542CEDC3F0875AD842E4DC7F9_A_M_Idl: I'd miss human feelings. The wind on my face, the smell of rain, dreams.
Dialogue.88F342E94BF985769A1604B0016A5783_A_P_Idl: But, what if that body had receptors for all of those things?
Dialogue.643E68D04E2C565FBBCD228109738DF5_A_M_Idl: I already have a body like that.
Dialogue.39A754F3458ED83A039F1EB1557275A3_A_P_Idl: You know full well what I mean!
Dialogue.E2D4A010473F7703AEF3DFA1C4003C9D_A_E_Idl: Sam, have you been off Earth before?
Dialogue.7BDC0389432D2A3D965D1583C3585605_A_M_Idl: No, this is my first trip into space. And a very distant one.
Dialogue.3350608941235BB72F88B1BE513AE1C0_A_E_Idl: I bet the change in gravity is giving you problems?
Dialogue.6033B54A4E804CC118B6C992DEC1E590_A_M_Idl: A bit. Everything's a little different…
Dialogue.D0644963468252E834B19F9791F68A7E_A_E_Idl: You'll get used to it. The spacesuit is like a second skin to me now!
Dialogue.4E5CF8124C623E9314F51EAD2C135E29_A_M_Idl: Maeve, I'm really impressed by your skills. Where did you learn your trade?
Dialogue.CB25A35C4F3783DABAEABE820C870B78_A_E_Idl: On the Moon, Mars… but mainly from my dad!
Dialogue.143C0C004A7736A83A7FBB97CCE67ADA_A_E_Idl: Only on Earth… Dad's afraid of flying through space, but he could fix a spaceship in mid-air!
Dialogue.82AD1155486F70C477F0EA98A602391B_A_M_Idl: When the temperature isn't going wild, this planet can be really beautiful.
Dialogue.93D052F94AE01704D7FB0EB554A468B1_A_E_Idl: Yeah… Earth doesn't have these beautiful landscapes untouched by humans anymore.
Dialogue.0599D7E4424DDD52DCE689976AF4B3E6_A_E_Idl: If my parents were to see me now…
Dialogue.9255CD9E4A58D2D74CC9C584EAB4C898_A_E_Idl: They'd be disappointed that I wasted my potential.
Dialogue.BBD8412F46D2F8FE473845B33C264A5F_A_M_Idl: You've got a doctorate! You're a doctor!
Dialogue.7BC974CC496BD0E4C7401EA605050534_A_E_Idl: I'm a prisoner working off his debt on a godforsaken planet.
Dialogue.97273B41416DA576CBFE9892496B6D2E_A_M_Idl: Minor details. I'm sure they still love you.
Dialogue.665ACFED41127D30E68846B00F673E89_A_E_Idl: Hmph...it's nice that you think so.
Dialogue.852F7B304D9E490BF477EC80E74EA803_A_M_Idl: You're quiet… When it was quiet at my house, that meant one of the kids got into trouble.
Dialogue.B6886A4C486177E11933BCA9AB17F0C3_A_E_Idl: You could afford a big family?
Dialogue.CC95804049C778462CF22AB59B05EC7A_A_M_Idl: Afford, shmafford… The more of us the merrier!
Dialogue.7E1DE024468D7D8253B652B1F820B7E7_A_M_Idl: Maeve, what do you miss the most?
Dialogue.C19DEFD34BE12C02C017F48B8C82D23D_A_M_Idl: They have the same algae bars back on Earth as anywhere else…
Dialogue.39CB825C4E6CB7DFB24DAA988D758B70_A_E_Idl: The women in my family are able to cook anything from nothing! Not me, I've got grease on my fingers, but you really need to try my Aunt Alyta's cooking!
Dialogue.BBA5EFED4CA0FB92FFBFF1A93489E3D7_A_E_Idl: Alright, Sam. Three things that you like here the most.
Dialogue.8A8D60274AF4BFC3C562A5BA48D62F8E_A_M_Idl: Hmm. Untouched nature, no IRO looking over our shoulder and the fact that we have some influence over our own fate, at least in some small way. What about you?
Dialogue.5773B810479C627557DBB6984818345D_A_E_Idl: First of all: Unlimited access to equipment. Second: The nature's not too bad. Third: Talking to one-third of my team.
Dialogue.3F63A7034C7EA80D33C72A98DFD8D3EC_A_E_Idl: Wow! Don't flatter yourself. I meant Han. Nothing gets a girl going like quoting military protocol.
Dialogue.FB28A10F44F5EEAE46F3F0915A94E507_A_E_Idl: Compared to the Moon colony, working here is almost kind of nice!
Dialogue.3C61FC6D4211BC5804FD0DB1CC5F0DA6_A_M_Idl: I do have to admit that, despite all of the unpleasantness, I do like it here too.
Dialogue.CC92EBD4485080C5505EB4A1C7AE749E_A_E_Idl: I never thought I'd say this, but it does seem like bloodthirsty aliens and exploding stars are better than colony overseers.
Dialogue.E75172EC416C88382D51499C19B3CD04_A_M_Idl: Only people can create real hell for other people.
Dialogue.9F62E0A6415525D8D70BD28BCC4FC2F0_A_E_Idl: Sam, can I ask you a personal question?
Dialogue.91CE21954F342CF0C6035191F2A8751F_A_E_Idl: What did they sentence you for?
Dialogue.D8E707344A930A1C5D11FE8D5DCD527A_A_M_Idl: I'm sure you've read my files.
Dialogue.B5A4E0DD4E304C5EBD41A5B307536B71_A_E_Idl: They mentioned terrorism. You don't look like a terrorist to me. You seem almost sad whenever you have to shoot the Vermin.
Dialogue.1061178443DF197E75E768AF7DE5B90A_A_M_Idl: Terrorism has many faces and you can support a cause without resorting to violence. I'm sure you know a little something about that.
Dialogue.AEBA25BF40271D70FC35DEB2A10400EA_A_E_Idl: Hey, Chris, I heard you've got three doctorates.
Dialogue.11388EBC4EC24134D29292A4EA875B5D_A_E_Idl: What do you need three scientific titles for? Wouldn't you have rather focused on your work?
Dialogue.3D6461A945948B89DD26E2930F298901_A_P_Idl: I see you're not familiar with the world of academia. Doctorates open many doors. They increase the probability my publications will get quoted and I have access to a broader spectrum of theoretical knowledge. Plus I did them all at once.
Dialogue.B4425756492067816DE756861736E910_A_P_Idl: And that's why you ended up as someone who does the dirty work.
Dialogue.569D1453454BB0463BD973B2DC34C069_A_E_Idl: I'll remind you that you're also here on this planet doing the same thing as me.
Dialogue.D4FF5E3541D0C1B72EA42DA780105B6E_A_P_Idl: But with a completely different mentality!
Dialogue.3032225541A2B13C3B55F99A234242DB_A_P_Idl: Maeve, what do you think of the technical resources for this mission?
Dialogue.F66E398645CB69EEFEE60DA62DED3A28_A_E_Idl: They're amazing! All of these printed buildings are frickin' awesome. It's too bad we can't play with all of them right away.
Dialogue.554302E249471267168662B8DA06F284_A_P_Idl: I have to admit I'm also rather impressed.
Dialogue.E79DF12E4F43B72BC12FEBB39BECD0A8_A_P_Idl: It's been years since I've seen my mother… or abuela. Do you miss your family, Chris?
Dialogue.E1C8A31B410B2EFDF0500AAD234172C8_A_E_Idl: I don't think about them at all. I need to focus on my research!
Dialogue.5EFE5EC44E4F9FB57FD0C691539BD1E3_A_P_Idl: You wouldn't want to see your mother?
Dialogue.BB26B7C54D74D1159EB0F1929BADC819_A_E_Idl: What for? She wouldn't understand my work anyway.
Dialogue.3E808D134A2DA915CB7912A7E3BDD088_A_P_Idl: Family is to get you away from work.
Dialogue.012769AB48AF74BBA5ECB5A9E5CBFEBD_A_P_Idl: I still can't believe I'm here! What an incredible place!
Dialogue.D7A5E8684610C672797744810A456326_A_E_Idl: Good to know at least one of us is happy…
Dialogue.80DC77FA48B72A33AE01F69556207B80_A_E_Idl: Chris, why did the Vermin cross the road?
Dialogue.122F8B9B40EBDAC115694C859C06AA00_A_P_Idl: What? There are no roads here…
Dialogue.9FA1AAF94E1CB94C7FB10DACBDEEAEF1_A_E_Idl: Because it already ate all of the street lights and some idiot turned on a flashlight!
Dialogue.F799B94B4356B62050F6E8BCA7B6C6FD_A_P_Idl: Flashlight batteries are too weak of a power source, they wouldn't have attracted the Vermin.
Dialogue.041C60174AADDB939151199E975D3506_A_E_Idl: I'm trying to tell you a joke.
Dialogue.893E4B0343F7EDBC80388E87BD2DD564_A_E_Idl: You come up with a better one then.
Dialogue.485B5A1D4A0BFAC0FD65959274D1AB85_A_P_Idl: Have you heard about the bacteria discovered at the bottom of a dormant volcano on Mars?
Dialogue.5D6C4BD54A693D58B8595FA9498D5A85_A_P_Idl: Oh. You didn't follow what the local laboratory was doing?
Dialogue.E2A95D2442801264D125A7B81CC57566_A_E_Idl: I was too busy building the lab modules. What was happening inside wasn't part of my job.
Dialogue.D1FDC48643CE1F50DE0BFFB09B39F693_A_P_Idl: Then maybe you're at least familiar with the work of Dr. Nguyen from the Moon University?
Dialogue.6E3C951D4530F33FC2F5C08634D3C509_A_E_Idl: I spent my last years on the Moon working off my punishment! You've got a strange idea of what convict life is like.
Dialogue.B94869C349DC4F9B485C2B82B951900E_A_E_Idl: When I was a kid I found a crashed police drone. My dad showed me how to fix it. That was my favorite toy!
Dialogue.AB17E5F94C63840771509EA520C20CCF_A_P_Idl: Once, out of curiosity, I took apart our microwave. My parents weren't happy. I increased its power efficiency and they didn't even thank me.
Dialogue.2FD1228646DB673BDA785FA468C0BE4F_A_P_Idl: Maeve, as a visitor to both celestial objects, which do you think is harder to colonize - the Moon or Mars?
Dialogue.D1A5AF2742C95F92AA3FCE8BD31BACFF_A_E_Idl: Hmm… Materials from Earth reach the Moon faster. But Mars has higher gravity and a real chance at being terraformed.
Dialogue.EB5B30464779550D9706C9907D760531_A_P_Idl: I think the Moon should only be an outpost on the way further out into space.
Dialogue.C4C569C1401338D16F0CDA9E621633BB_A_E_Idl: Don't forget it's also the source of Helium-3 for everything else.
Dialogue.A56F05DE4BF6F99C061625983561A4DA_A_E_Idl: Alright, Chris, that's enough. What were you convicted of?
Dialogue.254309E94FE0D143F0C7D9A2B5873ACF_A_E_Idl: I'd like to know if I'm stuck on the same planet as a psychopath that makes masks out of the skin of the victims he ate.
Dialogue.8482261042686E659F32258AF8254DC5_A_M_Idl: Then I have a question. How can you sleep knowing everything you had to do in the name of the IRO?
Dialogue.15DB37194AB9F28E02D6D09CDB13BB38_A_S_Idl: I don't sleep too well, but not because of the orders I carried out but because of the ones I didn't.
Dialogue.AE81A4F343F80303735FC0ADBD615A23_A_M_Idl: So even after your sentencing you're still on their side.
Dialogue.C46F523344260C6AA555AEAF6758E70F_A_S_Idl: No, I'm on our side. All of us. The side of peace.
Dialogue.AFFF101849CB54CA691659A20BD63C49_A_M_Idl: We are not going to be friends.
Dialogue.8EEAF8464FCC77834A1556B5548CF743_A_S_Idl: Biologist, as an expert in that field, you must find the Vermin interesting.
Dialogue.DBC9654642D5F9AAB5659F85C04C0F99_A_M_Idl: They've evolved and survived in extreme conditions… they understand Arcadia much better than we do.
Dialogue.D79B685B4730A91412EE3D938850B867_A_S_Idl: We'll be the ones to conquer it in the end.
Dialogue.A917F9864643F711DD0BEAAE5734D037_A_S_Idl: Why did you choose a career in the military?
Dialogue.6482BA6B4FBD2B9D3932D4AB2FE803C8_A_M_Idl: My father was a soldier. As was his father. My aunt's a cop and my cousin's in special forces…
Dialogue.6C24088E4A3BAEC98C4853A3A988FE50_A_S_Idl: So oppressing people is a family tradition?
Dialogue.78836C0843DD9DEB729443894B103E1C_A_M_Idl: Yes. We drink discipline and courage with our mother's milk!
Dialogue.768052B340940CCD9CF3DE8C3D7CB67E_A_S_Idl: The aliens are almost as annoying as the terrorists.
Dialogue.F0D37128448357161CC49783E69F2138_A_M_Idl: The resistance movement believes there's a better way to organize the world…
Dialogue.4DB617924882F6D7610CA9AC651FB724_A_S_Idl: They're animals that only know how to destroy.
Dialogue.8596E94347815FBAAACB8E9460F771C5_A_M_Idl: Their methods can be brutal, but the ideas behind them…
Dialogue.E002D02C4B7D4E845631AF80378B3C1C_A_S_Idl: You know nothing about life, doc.
Dialogue.47B79CA94D01E611428081BEE162FDE7_A_M_Idl: A friend of mine was an army doctor.
Dialogue.DD6C47D7453CE42A293831A186A78A9D_A_M_Idl: No, he treated people for real. He resigned when sleeves were introduced.
Dialogue.6F7517EB4548B88F297CC59267E18564_A_S_Idl: Makes sense. A soldier can't waste time on getting better. A new sleeve and he's back in the fight.
Dialogue.44F4B64647C53BA038E4FC8BBF16363A_A_M_Idl: My friend used to say that, in a way, that's more cruel than amputating someone's leg.
Dialogue.A2C757AE40FCFEFCF09C68BBF1271833_A_S_Idl: It's calm… I hope it's not the calm before the storm.
Dialogue.A44E0C804CF08C3CB1260FBCD2D77C46_A_M_Idl: For once I agree with you.
Dialogue.59267CE44412B23C6C8D05B8E6636FCD_A_M_Idl: Han, don't you see the irony?
Dialogue.087DF78443F868A01336779366A93A4A_A_M_Idl: You love the IRO so much, you're a good little soldier, and yet you ended up here, on an alien planet along with three other convicts who hate the system. How did that happen?
Dialogue.CEAFD95A439E84C06095498C664F5C71_A_S_Idl: A just system does not play favorites. I deserve my punishment and I'm grateful for the opportunity to atone.
Dialogue.EB5FF05C4A72B709283E5DAEC6EC141B_A_S_Idl: Samuel, what did the IRO do that was so bad?
Dialogue.2175663E417650099E6E99BC74823487_A_M_Idl: Where do I start? It enslaved the world, it erodes basic human rights, it hands all natural resources over to the corporations. And it monopolized immortality.
Dialogue.C5E2E8EB4104BAD90D923BB24C60E47F_A_S_Idl: Just what I thought. Nothing concrete, just your propaganda.
Dialogue.25AB686D45401966F7C41398ED06E5C4_A_M_Idl: Our propaganda? I've seen parents being sent off to other planets because they decided to have a child! I've seen young people being sent to penal colonies because they needed sleeves for their loved ones! I could go on and on.
Dialogue.FED44B344D537A62426F97BF969FBA2F_A_S_Idl: Typical. You see human tragedy and blame the government instead of seeing the big picture.
Dialogue.F43FD15C4AB00533A8DC288B309E244C_A_M_Idl: I'm not talking about this anymore.
Dialogue.4DA498E6406367B974F93C98B733EFA1_A_M_Idl: It's quiet. You can take a break if you want.
Dialogue.7B5846BD40EDEE6C6925D48DFF29C507_A_P_Idl: Hey, S8466, how should I address you?
Dialogue.FDEE607E400ED7190FE468B42089DA17_A_P_Idl: Yes, but I have more of them!
Dialogue.9E6A196D447696EFF00FDC9B6A9CE783_A_S_Idl: Doctor, do you see anything we should be worried about?
Dialogue.5B0C234041CE5D677CE7CAABD9EE9A6F_A_P_Idl: That's your job… I don't have time to pay attention to things like that.
Dialogue.9AB9CC454C6A39703E5E988EC919E980_A_P_Idl: What's death when we have sleeves? But losing time is definitely a setback…
Dialogue.9901B6C94F2866F575C3038461D509FF_A_S_Idl: If we could capture a Slasher alive…
Dialogue.ADAA732D4F973A7EE32A2991FFDD26F2_A_P_Idl: I could hook it up to the apparatus and study its reactions…
Dialogue.3396A44340A93BA56ADCB28D6B2DFB7B_A_S_Idl: Security protocols would not allow it.
Dialogue.817A6BCB44EC883F4834158D436A1EC2_A_S_Idl: Find a different path to fame.
Dialogue.E971BD7540D3121C2211AFB798723DB0_A_P_Idl: It's not about fame, it's about science.
Dialogue.8C992EB948DE6D5D9764E38BC1A0CCC6_A_P_Idl: Doctor, is there any point to your research? Does it change anything?
Dialogue.D9F2B2FA4410ECADBB69A7AB894F9AC3_A_S_Idl: For example, if we understand how the Rift works, we'll be able to open more of them and reach other galaxies!
Dialogue.7CA3A4DB449721214D24879574DCFD45_A_P_Idl: What if we encounter other civilizations?
Dialogue.FE5CED844E051109AF0EED8191C90AC2_A_S_Idl: Then that's a job for people like you, not scientists.
Dialogue.D2112E5F47724355F339DF8B1444E91C_A_S_Idl: Hey, Sergeant. Have you ever considered a more fulfilling career path?
Dialogue.E8B5C28F4C3F82B9141ECF96229CCC80_A_P_Idl: Have you ever considered shutting up?
Dialogue.E4FA675B46BA3E78616EACBC665293AA_A_S_Idl: Why so angry? As an individual soldier you don't have any impact on anything that could move the world forward. You don't mind being a cog in a machine?
Dialogue.35993B9E4EDCAEA95F5BA881D57EB16B_A_P_Idl: No. It's not a career, it's a duty.
Dialogue.985D774246E4ED20B8CE6697C4FF51D9_A_S_Idl: Okay then. Keep shooting at stuff, as long as it brings in money for research.
Dialogue.7870FFC2463CCFBF86BC53B488E2F511_A_S_Idl: After talking to Maeve, I've decided it'll be easier if we address each other by our first names.
Dialogue.8FA0D49147AD3B49F6FC8A99999CD9F6_A_P_Idl: Makes sense, our first names have less syllables. It'll significantly speed up communication.
Dialogue.2EA40D754434475588B4D6BF50A1C34E_A_P_Idl: Han, did you know that a projectile fired from your weapon from 300 meters will hit the target with a force…
Dialogue.90BE579E4735B520181A6887EBBD3267_A_S_Idl: Strong enough to obliterate the enemy.
Dialogue.09BA210E4EF3EFDED99F4AB53CCB4839_A_S_Idl: I know how to shoot. I don't need to know the theory.
Dialogue.B7003BEA4253CA746E2739AB40545C77_A_P_Idl: That was my last attempt at small talk.
Dialogue.CDEC07CA4A04FE4C0B4CECB444212827_A_P_Idl: Han, I was wondering. What does someone like you think of scientific progress?
Dialogue.2E01F9BB425E7FA9E562959F4A9FF1F3_A_S_Idl: What do you mean "someone like me"?
Dialogue.43F5F9E243EE3B97477F72975B26F7E1_A_S_Idl: Euphemisms are not your strong suit.
Dialogue.D4EF2C9F4D2C8384960C268FC49E7F25_A_P_Idl: Oh, that's not an invention. I'm talking about something that moved the world and mankind's understanding forward.
Dialogue.7ED7E29E42B640E73231859BD00B19F1_A_S_Idl: That's still the IRO. Combining all nations into one stopped most wars and that allowed for things like colonizing the solar system. That was not possible in less certain times.
Dialogue.786F283045F03E590A287FBE8FC9F5DE_A_S_Idl: E4101, you look like you're a magnet for trouble.
Dialogue.748334784B09B3E25052DBACA071189A_A_E_Idl: Hey, Han. Why do you have that metal plate in your head? Would’ve been cheaper to print a sleeve with a full skull.
Dialogue.17A244C541A25D81EB1B16A22E9B31B2_A_E_Idl: Oh, so it's some kind of enhancement? Like an LEM or something? I don’t really know much about that stuff. Maybe I should get one too? Memory problems run in my family. My grandpa once forgot to pick me up from school — I had to spend the night hiding in the janitor’s closet so we wouldn’t get fined.
Dialogue.85AA9A1D4C3CEEC36D55998B961C3E9B_A_S_Idl: It’s just a cranial prosthesis. It doesn’t enhance brain function. It, uh... helps me to remember my mistakes.
Dialogue.DB0BE86B4657C86458C95D9929C73895_A_E_Idl: I won't pretend I'm a saint. I've helped smuggle this and that in my time for..."those in need".
Dialogue.AE838CE04F97BF70059872AEC2B9224A_A_S_Idl: People like you don't understand order. You just cause more problems for everyone else.
Dialogue.4F940FD34032B0212E605ABAE1DE31D0_A_E_Idl: And you always followed orders and ended up in the exact same place as I did. I'd rather not follow anyone and be free!
Dialogue.86F7555040B8EC6B4FEBE882797ABB37_A_S_Idl: I'd prefer it if you addressed me using my rank.
Dialogue.B51FCA88400C5CE4E2C62AA63757EA9B_A_E_Idl: Don't you think that makes communication more difficult? There's only four of us here. Who are you trying to impress?
Dialogue.F037A480453EE688B18416B11D2D3FD3_A_S_Idl: I'm not. I've worked hard for my rank.
Dialogue.CC8A0668495367D872D67EB9502FC6AF_A_E_Idl: So, Han, how about taking a little break?
Dialogue.3E32E3294BD3061CBA3F849D9EE8597D_A_E_Idl: That sounded like a yes to me. Great.
Dialogue.175C32B14134A013D449FE9C97D4ED00_A_S_Idl: I've been thinking a lot lately.
Dialogue.3AE4555344D18E2C16735BB93AB4076C_A_S_Idl: We're stuck here as a small group. In unusual circumstances, the protocol allows for more direct ways of addressing one another…
Dialogue.39805AED4AD0D2F69E9D02A751B89F6E_A_E_Idl: So I can call you Han?
Dialogue.0BC1429E4928687267652291583DAE22_A_E_Idl: I'm just kidding. That's what friends do, Han!
Dialogue.0790F61949D408049D770BA683ACED63_A_S_Idl: I was asking about you. You've been quiet lately…
Dialogue.F3FABCF246A6BFC6D665C2B56251B6E9_A_S_Idl: A person can start feeling lonely out in space… If you ever need someone to talk to, let me know.
Dialogue.6D43AFF8408D7C5673FF408FA4D5FDDC_A_S_Idl: Maeve, you've worked on the Moon, right? Did you know any of the army guys there?
Dialogue.66253298408591BBBAC44BBDCC1FF164_A_E_Idl: I once went on a date with one… turned out to be a real boy scout, like every guy in uniform. No offense.
Dialogue.B1A5EA6148FAFCDEBD316DBF83499693_A_E_Idl: Oh, come on, we gotta talk about something while we work. I'll start. I spy with my little eye a giant ball of hot deadly gas.
Dialogue.AFBE9A974136AF2E443176B84794D2D2_A_E_Idl: Cheese and crackers, you're so booriiing.
Dialogue.8D76B7B04D6182E0DB3076B630F73F68_A_S_Idl: There's too many eggheads and not enough soldiers on these missions. A trained squad with good gear could properly secure the base.
Dialogue.3E65213E4DAB9FC5D561CD9B49E0BFB1_A_E_Idl: Not all problems can be solved with violence.
Dialogue.CEE73DE948BFE0DDEB991C93F7FB95B5_A_S_Idl: You wanna be friends with the Vermin?
Dialogue.B13F50B148C93A972B2B19B121DD1C52_A_E_Idl: What if we create a deterrence system? Or neutralize the magnetic field around power sources?
Dialogue.E5DC80F64684539789D731A849269C01_A_S_Idl: You should be talking to the phys…. Chris about that, not me.
Dialogue.401CF379408D0F2992DAC1BE2C443A85_A_E_Idl: Hey Han, did you ever go to "Joey's" on the Moon?
Dialogue.84549A5A49FA98EA959C308E68D7D711_A_S_Idl: To that dump? Soldiers went to the "Blind Crab".
Dialogue.1F8DCB1F495B1C0C0E998CBB03F903A9_A_E_Idl: And that's why no one else went there! You soldiers don't even know the taste of real proper moonshine!
Dialogue.E6D5539B482A322E7371CD886B5A1A7B_A_S_Idl: Maeve. Can I ask you a personal question?
Dialogue.BDA0B40D48386D14B055E8949EAFD97C_A_E_Idl: I won't answer any other kind.
Dialogue.4F3FE70B462FB3D1E2C39C86D5F10A3E_A_S_Idl: You can swear all you want as far as I'm concerned.
Dialogue.A2B666064FFC3636CDDDFBA7D083FA91_A_E_Idl: Sorry, you don't make the rules here.
Dialogue.A981964E4DD325FA64C2AF8C15014203_A_S_Idl: Why do you always say things like cheese and crackers or gosh darn it?
Dialogue.EB06DDBD44EE1271A349539C965A45A6_A_E_Idl: I have no idea what you're talking about.
Dialogue.89F3EE064E784E1A275ACDAE879E381D_A_E_Idl: Where I'm from, everyone used to curse like a sailor and it's hard to get rid of old habits.
Dialogue.4080CC534D7C0CFFF6F7229775C63690_A_S_Idl: Why get rid of them at all?
Dialogue.D73F32994A5724E7E3EA15B780054CA1_A_E_Idl: In certain places they can lead to unpleasantness.
Dialogue.EA69F8154733E42A0FB6E1B9E8EC66CB_A_S_Idl: I see. Rules are rules. But in my squad you could always swear as much as you wanted.
Dialogue.D5A986F34C3EE2274A03209442D80205_A_E_Idl: That's the difference. In your squad you made the rules. In the places I was at, people like you often made the rules for everyone else.
Dialogue.8B3478B149AA6A3D9F16529DF481B7CD_A_E_Idl: Gal, I wanted to send a message to my sister. Is that possible?
Dialogue.8B3478B149AA6A3D9F16529DF481B7CD_A_M_Idl: Gal, can we ask for more supplies?
Dialogue.8B3478B149AA6A3D9F16529DF481B7CD_A_P_Idl: Gal, do I have access to the Doctor's research…
Dialogue.E0DE9ECB4D001E74B7CA3FAC8A61075D_A_G_Idl: Your rights were written down and presented to you as appendix 6A in your contract.
Dialogue.1901F6B44207DE9E033EB0BDF8530069_A_E_Idl: I love these backpacks. Before pocket technology, I had to lug kilos of junk around with me. That gets tiring even in Martian gravity.
Dialogue.1901F6B44207DE9E033EB0BDF8530069_A_M_Idl: You gotta give Claywood credit, these backpacks are amazing.
Dialogue.1901F6B44207DE9E033EB0BDF8530069_A_P_Idl: It's incredible how much can fit into these backpacks. I can't imagine going back to a time before pocket technology.
Dialogue.1901F6B44207DE9E033EB0BDF8530069_A_S_Idl: When I started my service, we didn't have extradimensional backpacks. We had to carry everything on our backs.
Dialogue.8DB11BB6425DD7DC5E4B87A664726393_A_E_Idl: Hey, Gal, what's it like being an artificial intelligence?
Dialogue.8DB11BB6425DD7DC5E4B87A664726393_A_M_Idl: Gal. You really don't remember anything, do you?
Dialogue.8DB11BB6425DD7DC5E4B87A664726393_A_P_Idl: Gal, what's the temperature of Arcadia-7's core?
Dialogue.8DB11BB6425DD7DC5E4B87A664726393_A_S_Idl: Gal, I've assumed command here, but I don't feel like I'm really fulfilling that role.
Dialogue.ACCD22554147DCE23351298C53240C2E_A_G_E_I: That is impossible to answer. It's like trying to explain to a dog what it's like to be human.
Dialogue.ACCD22554147DCE23351298C53240C2E_A_G_M_I: Of course I remember. My database encompasses virtually all of mankind's knowledge.
Dialogue.DDFAE2B440899BB5CEC333848B0BA4C4_A_E_Idl: I'm like a dog to you?
Dialogue.DDFAE2B440899BB5CEC333848B0BA4C4_A_M_Idl: You don't remember anything from the time when we used to work together?
Dialogue.DDFAE2B440899BB5CEC333848B0BA4C4_A_S_Idl: All orders go through you. Plus I don't really have any concrete methods of persuasion.
Dialogue.06B5F3D54C8ADE7EC10BEE912749C875_A_G_E_I: I mean that our thought processes are not comparable. You're not like a dog at all.
Dialogue.06B5F3D54C8ADE7EC10BEE912749C875_A_G_M_I: Of course, I remember everything. I feel like you just signed the mission contract yesterday.
Dialogue.06B5F3D54C8ADE7EC10BEE912749C875_A_G_S_I: S8466, remember that you have been legally convicted, we cannot allow you into the system.
Dialogue.BEC48D4A43CC1433D24B54A5EA37C488_A_E_Idl: At all? I'm not friendly or loyal in your eyes?
Dialogue.BEC48D4A43CC1433D24B54A5EA37C488_A_M_Idl: Gal, I'm talking about the distant past. About the start of the Claywood Corporation.
Dialogue.BEC48D4A43CC1433D24B54A5EA37C488_A_P_Idl: It's always better to be sure.
Dialogue.BEC48D4A43CC1433D24B54A5EA37C488_A_S_Idl: Then why did I assume that role if you're really the one in charge?
Dialogue.509B38C34A9A7EB419662D999092375A_A_G_E_I: You are. What I mean is that I respect you, like all employees of the Claywood Corporation.
Dialogue.509B38C34A9A7EB419662D999092375A_A_G_M_I: I did not exist when the company was founded. Mr. Claywood created me relatively recently. But I can tell you about the company's beginnings.
Dialogue.509B38C34A9A7EB419662D999092375A_A_G_P_I: How could you? I'm an advanced artificial intelligence, capable of things your protein-based brain has never even dreamed of.
Dialogue.509B38C34A9A7EB419662D999092375A_A_G_S_I: Because you're human. We can't allow an AI to lead the mission. That would look very bad. From a marketing perspective.
Dialogue.BE70FA6246A4FAD0DE07B08411CB2128_A_E_Idl: Gal, this Claywood, what's he like?
Dialogue.BE70FA6246A4FAD0DE07B08411CB2128_A_M_Idl: Gal, don't you feel underappreciated? You're incredibly capable, yet your role boils down to being an assistant.
Dialogue.BE70FA6246A4FAD0DE07B08411CB2128_A_P_Idl: Gal, the chemical formula for biofilament.
Dialogue.BE70FA6246A4FAD0DE07B08411CB2128_A_S_Idl: Gal, how many veterans have been to Arcadia-7 so far?
Dialogue.D0F835074CB7B3136AF399A0EAF080E5_A_G_E_I: Mr. Claywood is a genius, philanthropist and billionaire. A fighter for humanity…
Dialogue.D0F835074CB7B3136AF399A0EAF080E5_A_G_M_I: No. Just because I take care of you doesn't mean I'm not doing a million other things as well. It's just one copy of my personality on Arcadia.
Dialogue.D0F835074CB7B3136AF399A0EAF080E5_A_G_P_I: What about the chemical formula for biofilament?
Dialogue.D0F835074CB7B3136AF399A0EAF080E5_A_G_S_I: Ever since the Vermin were discovered, there's been more and more of them. No one was worried about such things during earlier missions.
Dialogue.ED8C2AB64465A11AAF8A4D901F420A94_A_E_Idl: Don't quote the omnipedia. What's he like? As a person?
Dialogue.ED8C2AB64465A11AAF8A4D901F420A94_A_M_Idl: Okay, but you could definitely command the entire mission instead of taking orders from some fat cats at the top.
Dialogue.ED8C2AB64465A11AAF8A4D901F420A94_A_P_Idl: Give it to me. I'm working on something and I forgot it.
Dialogue.ED8C2AB64465A11AAF8A4D901F420A94_A_S_Idl: So the first missions were doomed to fail.
Dialogue.B8A0E07B4A7D6B3B8E6C1390C394F391_A_G_E_I: Recording stopped. He's difficult. Good. But difficult.
Dialogue.B8A0E07B4A7D6B3B8E6C1390C394F391_A_G_M_I: That's not my objective. Everyone here has their tasks. Space missions need order.
Dialogue.B8A0E07B4A7D6B3B8E6C1390C394F391_A_G_S_I: Notice that the presence of the military did not result in spectacular successes for subsequent missions.
Dialogue.46E84D6A4265AB98D6985B8CEF86F380_A_P_Idl: Don't start with me. Give me the formula.
Dialogue.0266FA3549E7F8BE88C4A8955F3DA4F0_A_G_P_I: You don't need it right now for what you're supposed to be doing.
Dialogue.753A283042FDC3827D0747A2DF4565DC_A_P_Idl: And this is why we're not moving forward! You could've given me the formula and we could've invented something wonderful. But you'd rather waste my time.
Dialogue.BC9561634C42CF44A501A894681CF90E_A_G_P_I: In regards to wasting time, you used 130 times more energy and time to say those words than you would've used to simply say "please".
Dialogue.3C532DDC48FFFAAB8760E7BFE661DDD6_A_E_Idl: Gal, I was wondering, what's the real probability of us paying off our debt and going back home?
Dialogue.3C532DDC48FFFAAB8760E7BFE661DDD6_A_M_Idl: Gal. What do you like the most about this place?
Dialogue.F7624EA7469B44205D0FEFAF2A8B5B64_A_G_E_I: Too many variables. I'm not able to calculate that.
Dialogue.6564820F481AD203134E6884AC1349BF_A_E_Idl: I was hoping you'd cheer me up.
Dialogue.EF39B3D04CE43681FEE8858E4FFCB7FD_A_G_Idl: I see. In that case, the probability of you paying off your debt is 100%.
I see. In that case, the probability of you paying off your debt is 100%.
Dialogue.C2DC72654581C7406EBF6D9638AE66C1_A_M_Idl: You've never liked the night. You always woke up at dawn. As if you never wanted to waste a single moment of sunlight.
Dialogue.A3BBADFA4D8DBC768FFD0D9574E626F2_A_M_Idl: Why did you become an engineer?
Dialogue.895B72F649DF033FE696FCA42DCBA21C_A_S_Idl: You should've stayed with them then. Why'd you choose to work out in space?
Dialogue.B9ACF0B446BD6568BA09BA87E701DD88_A_S_Idl: If money's more important to you than family then you have no right to complain now.
Dialogue.31ECEF254319D8436D4954BC9A76562F_A_E_Idl: You think that money was for me?! I sent everything back home, you prick!
Dialogue.BDB9F50A4F0B35319368AFB75FAE4E0D_A_M_Idl: Han? Soldiers often suffer from PTSD. Psychology is not really my forte but…
Dialogue.D3E0E7DE4CFA940F5B5511BAF1B5BA93_A_S_Idl: Then you shouldn't speak on the subject.
Dialogue.886E544C4273504152C2C687EE810D76_A_M_Idl: We can talk if you want.
Dialogue.EB90A6884522F24613C242831CC00E2E_A_S_Idl: The military is not for the weak. I don't have any trauma.
Dialogue.538C40164AC3698D8AB21D9CC33177C5_A_E_Idl: Doc… You can't help someone who doesn't want to be helped.
Dialogue.BAA3DDA3409182E8A3AF9186FEDE3E4D_A_M_Idl: I had to at least try.
Dialogue.DF340DCB45BECBB3FDA801BF6C07D03C_A_E_Idl: I like to know how things work. To take them apart and put them back together so that they work again. I got that from my dad.
Dialogue.47BC7B9F488A12C542E593A53E0BB5BB_A_P_Idl: I agree! But machines are not enough, I want to understand how the entire universe works! That's why I'm here. To move science forward.
Dialogue.AEF0BA04416AA202133B61882144DE69_A_E_Idl: What about you, doc? Why medicine?
Dialogue.FE0C53034F56C6CEABE9F1A8DB3CF246_A_M_Idl: I always wanted to help people.
Dialogue.17AAF3824CD576E85401A2A9F4109FF5_A_E_Idl: Soldiers don't help anyone except those in charge…
Dialogue.325C12E94E7FBED3F01EFF9CB1E28475_A_M_Idl: We don't have to talk about politics right now.
Dialogue.6DA1CF984AFD7307310FC0B8E48DCD25_A_E_Idl: Every day we try not to die out here and there are some people just wishing for it…
Dialogue.B9EF17AE43D5E04F58ECA8A732902219_A_E_Idl: You've never heard of the Church of Immortality?
Dialogue.4D14890043B49137F3D94CB0E5D58456_A_P_Idl: That doesn't lie in my areas of interest.
Dialogue.CCB925E948985AFD7C6518A5E0C20A33_A_S_Idl: They believe that the fire waves are a test. If you survive them that means the aliens chose you.
Dialogue.BCC3322F4ACA28735BFC5FAB756638C7_A_M_Idl: Those people are just lost, they're trying to make sense of a world they don't understand…
Dialogue.6405FEA5470FD7B9197A4DAEF883CB75_A_E_Idl: I say we let them in here. Once a few of them burn to ash the rest will quickly smarten up.
Dialogue.101728E94509539401481DA20D4D148E_A_E_Idl: Alright, gentlemen, time to confess - which one of you has a chica back home waiting for her beloved to return from the edges of space?
Dialogue.5D3BF4F749693E74D047A7BDC6F8C579_A_M_Idl: I met a very nice girl at the penal colony… but I doubt she's waiting for me now.
Dialogue.8FB40E03488F82A6DC04898C3D9EF009_A_M_Idl: Her debt was small. She probably paid it off already and returned to her normal life.
Dialogue.3C6BC55948FCE71A8D1D70A668BA6CC9_A_S_Idl: I don't wanna talk about it.
Dialogue.BBE587714E4344C062F2CC90C7E266DA_A_P_Idl: Romance in the lab has a negative impact on the work. I never stooped to the level of some of my colleagues.
Dialogue.74AEB2C2445265ED3643FAA27CDCC679_A_E_Idl: That's pretty weak, gentlemen, pretty weak.
Dialogue.E1606CAB4B1601B83C733BB312AC114F_A_E_Idl: Do you know the last time I saw a live wild animal? Ages ago!
Dialogue.544DB72F435D6CC19069FCBDCAC29F5F_A_M_Idl: Flocks of birds would often fly over the penal colony. I liked watching them. They're free…
Dialogue.5A1EF6A1466EAEB848EA8C95F9903602_A_E_Idl: Birds! I'd kill to see a bird again!
Dialogue.A66DAFB34FA9F4E64B1CA6A3FC63CFAD_A_E_Idl: I heard they brought some to the Moon but I never saw them.
Dialogue.8DBC5EF4449D0FE0F3DE9A980D353553_A_P_Idl: I'm glad there are no birds here. They'd try building a nest in the machines, and would probably break something.
Dialogue.5EEF3D61494A21AACA849BB8B9EF9E16_A_E_Idl: I'm really not happy about what happened in the Forgotten Engine…
Dialogue.3A4542264B251C13329033B6F47EF11D_A_P_Idl: A terrible tragedy, I can't even believe it!
Dialogue.2B23872B49B760D7529B6EB7FB010F97_A_E_Idl: I didn't think you'd care this much…
Dialogue.AD4870B347857654CD5BA1926CEC77C8_A_P_Idl: How could someone just abandon such valuable research!
Dialogue.6E56B7DE4DA915E15EC16798BEC603B4_A_E_Idl: I was talking about the people…
Dialogue.6908DFD9486F81806E600E8A0ACEE80D_A_S_Idl: The people weren't properly trained. They made many mistakes while defending themselves.
Dialogue.727E53C04571E9D4057203A5904BFDF7_A_E_Idl: The corporations left them here to die! It wasn't their fault! You both have issues.
Dialogue.7670DBF04F19B22DF521C99173F051B4_A_E_Idl: Hey, Chris! You were on the Moon, right?
Dialogue.703DC85C48E242904B52B9A15C8A928C_A_E_Idl: That doesn't make sense. I thought you were fascinated by colonization.
Dialogue.0AE56A35445B72DD84AC2DBF18E1989D_A_P_Idl: My work was always about looking ahead! To send people beyond our tiny solar system! That's why I'm here!
Dialogue.A63C4FAA4C48E919D726A18F3BC8C8C4_A_S_Idl: You like starting off the deep end? I respect that.
Dialogue.0F7A5A69431BB5DD0920F9AB6933C950_A_E_Idl: What's life on Earth like now?
Dialogue.9E4F30A345B2A43D507C6B981F3B124E_A_P_Idl: I'm not sure what you're asking…
Dialogue.A6181466434479E309D620A09F4DE875_A_E_Idl: About everyday life. What's it like on Earth?
Dialogue.C2687D924DAA23C82813C0A64DFA7FBA_A_E_Idl: Did you ever set foot outside your lab?
Dialogue.4F59670F4EC6EF8C56E376A8BB2217EF_A_P_Idl: My work was about looking at the stars, not at my feet.
Dialogue.4290911E4D4FC0E261F91D817EB463B8_A_M_Idl: Well… I can only tell you from the perspective of the penal colony. It's definitely nice to have a stable star above your head.
Dialogue.8920D1244DCAE6A7775F6BA82B15E936_A_M_Idl: When I was a kid I never thought we'd ever leave Earth again… much less that I'd personally end up on an alien planet.
Dialogue.6C7E2E6E45E3331A7A0E0883A81442B9_A_S_Idl: It was normal that they'd send me to serve on the other side of the world, but the Moon? That was a great honor.
Dialogue.39455E744492D91690C9429EFDDBDCA5_A_P_Idl: I dreamt of space travel since I was a kid! Thanks to the discs, conquering space is now easier than ever!
Dialogue.570383F24830617F006884A60F50ED72_A_M_Idl: The discs have changed the world so much… who knows what it will look like in a hundred years.
Dialogue.830320FC42A1342E2C85B688D4388E4F_A_G_Inv: Due to your hard work we have decided to increase the capacity of your pockets. Your inventory has been updated and you can now fit more items into it.
Dialogue.5A9E1F68423A76FBC3CDE3A8B8DE5AC3_A_E_L_1: On a planet where everything can kill you, to die at the hands of your colleague is so…
Dialogue.5A9E1F68423A76FBC3CDE3A8B8DE5AC3_A_M_L_1: On a planet where everything can kill you, to die at the hands of your colleague is so…
Dialogue.5A9E1F68423A76FBC3CDE3A8B8DE5AC3_A_P_L_1: On a planet where everything can kill you, to die at the hands of your colleague is so…
Dialogue.5A9E1F68423A76FBC3CDE3A8B8DE5AC3_A_S_L_1: On a planet where everything can kill you, to die at the hands of your colleague is so…
Dialogue.A028F51F4D1192FEA5D3DBBF88AB3456_A_E_L_1: I was gonna say depressing. But I agree.
Dialogue.A028F51F4D1192FEA5D3DBBF88AB3456_A_M_L_1: I was gonna say sad. But I agree.
Dialogue.A028F51F4D1192FEA5D3DBBF88AB3456_A_P_L_1: I was gonna say ironic. But I agree.
Dialogue.A028F51F4D1192FEA5D3DBBF88AB3456_A_S_L_1: I was gonna say human. But I agree.
Dialogue.D384E662441CA3D35640D8B1AB89ADBA_A_E_L_1: This lock requires three separate keycards.
Dialogue.0F6ADA5F42CE149D2E721A9F78B2F433_A_E_L_1: The stench is unbelievable. Are you sure it's safe?
Dialogue.0F6ADA5F42CE149D2E721A9F78B2F433_A_P_L_1: I can still smell the hydrogen sulfide. Are you sure it's safe?
Dialogue.EC7FFE814CBCAB5028B1A49152E47B79_A_M_L_1: Most of the gas has dropped to the bottom, so if we keep to the upper part of the base we should be fine.
Dialogue.F686940B420BDA3B3049E3AB90CB7A55_A_E_L_2: Too bad the research didn't amount to anything.
Dialogue.F686940B420BDA3B3049E3AB90CB7A55_A_P_L_2: Research to help mankind. I need to read this Diaz's work.
Dialogue.F686940B420BDA3B3049E3AB90CB7A55_A_S_L_2: The Bloodfern was a good idea.
Dialogue.D10AC4BD4213115EEFFCD2996F4FC417_A_E_L_2: He was killed by his own virus.
Dialogue.887A4AB04331843C4CCA5788FC196992_A_E_L_2: He was saving his son, I get it, but still…
Dialogue.887A4AB04331843C4CCA5788FC196992_A_P_L_2: He sacrificed amazing research just to save one kid, that's absurd!
Dialogue.887A4AB04331843C4CCA5788FC196992_A_S_L_2: He attacked his own base. He would've been court martialed.
Dialogue.F9245E3C41C9B9E48C86D598ABC68617_A_E_L_2: This area could use a trim.
Dialogue.EF36F18F4971B7C8F9B9288F3378981B_A_P_Las: I need to analyze this fight.
Dialogue.A7AB3B004F2787FE312CEFBC5E28C6F3_A_P_Las: We can get back to work.
Dialogue.0AE54F9F443DCA72C6E6ED8513908A21_A_P_Lev: Learning is the key to greatness.
Dialogue.124BA6ED4FDE18A96A97C4A58763C21F_A_M_M_1: Where there's people there's prejudice. Poor girl.
Dialogue.124BA6ED4FDE18A96A97C4A58763C21F_A_P_M_1: That was senseless. If they had just thought for one second it would've been clear she was innocent.
Dialogue.492E03B24CB2856281F04ABFDF82A09E_A_E_M_2: I was wondering why we're using wolfram.
Dialogue.492E03B24CB2856281F04ABFDF82A09E_A_M_M_2: This planet keeps getting stranger and stranger.
Dialogue.492E03B24CB2856281F04ABFDF82A09E_A_P_M_2: The great mystery of the lack of copper. I need to look into this.
Dialogue.492E03B24CB2856281F04ABFDF82A09E_A_S_M_2: That explains why we're using wolfram.
Dialogue.657EB62D4A19C2B1DA1E5FB3475F1977_A_E_M_2: I knew it, we can't trust Claywood.
Dialogue.657EB62D4A19C2B1DA1E5FB3475F1977_A_P_M_2: Rightly so. Miller didn't fulfill his agreement.
Dialogue.657EB62D4A19C2B1DA1E5FB3475F1977_A_S_M_2: Claywood always seemed a little off to me.
Dialogue.992E63AF430AB8E6BB7D79AA6F3D8B12_A_E_M_3: It was too much for him.
Dialogue.992E63AF430AB8E6BB7D79AA6F3D8B12_A_S_M_3: He couldn't take it. There were people like that back in the army.
Dialogue.2489A12A4403CB4354ECB1AEDFF4778A_A_M_M_6: There are lines that shouldn't be crossed.
Dialogue.2489A12A4403CB4354ECB1AEDFF4778A_A_P_M_6: Not a bad idea. If FHS didn't poison the biofilament I'd eat it too.
Dialogue.2489A12A4403CB4354ECB1AEDFF4778A_A_S_M_6: They had no choice. I've seen people this desperate before.
Dialogue.4011B5CE4294D90AB06A1F9DE0C572FD_A_G_Map: You have successfully unlocked the geolocation service of structural and topological imaging.
Dialogue.7D68225349639738DDCB2D84236F967A_A_E_Map: Sounds like a complicated name for a map.
Dialogue.7D68225349639738DDCB2D84236F967A_A_M_Map: I assume it's some sort of a navigation system? A map?
Dialogue.7D68225349639738DDCB2D84236F967A_A_P_Map: Great! A map will be useful.
Dialogue.B2D4C77443A8DD387E77B1AC788713B1_A_G_Map: If you insist on using such primitive language, go ahead.
Dialogue.B9410E6E44A60BEAAD83029C70F5AC80_A_G_Moo: Delivered! The Moon Energy Corporation thanks you for your shipment! You can claim your reward in the Corporate Terminal!
Dialogue.00BCF62044370AAB0C52858F778EFF9D_A_G_Moo: Great work! The Moon Energy Corporation received its order! You can claim your rightful reward, as usual, in the Corporate Terminal. They are very happy with your services.
Dialogue.992F2554414D0DEF491AB091D92A7328_A_G_Moo: Congratulations, the Moon Energy Corporation is grateful for your shipment. Another reward is waiting for you in the terminal. I'd like to point out how clean the energy is that's produced by Moon Energy devices.
Dialogue.F2DE19A347D744067A0EBBB571821669_A_G_Moo: Moon Energy thanks you for another shipment! According to their observations, your production has not damaged the environment. The amount of greenhouse gases in Arcadia-7's atmosphere has not changed!
Dialogue.07F6E49C44F0D1D4A02D5EAD80448E5C_A_G_Moo: Moon Energy hopes that once you return to Earth, a hero and a pioneer, you will tell everyone all about that.
Dialogue.C5BA1A2A42B1C0C80349B3A638CB6AFA_A_E_Moo: Aren't the greenhouse gases in balance maybe because there's a giant start constantly exploding next to the planet?
Dialogue.C5BA1A2A42B1C0C80349B3A638CB6AFA_A_M_Moo: It's obvious our production has no impact on this planet's atmosphere. Ruptura's powerful explosions do.
Dialogue.C5BA1A2A42B1C0C80349B3A638CB6AFA_A_P_Moo: I'm not sure what I would say. Since our planet is constantly being hit by the explosions of a large star, our production has little, if not zero, influence on any atmospheric changes. There's literally nothing to tell.
Dialogue.C5BA1A2A42B1C0C80349B3A638CB6AFA_A_S_Moo: A huge star keeps incinerating the entire planet and we're supposed to worry about the environment?
Dialogue.335793334E856A9A5819918B424B4930_A_G_Moo: Great job! The Moon Energy Corporation thanks you for another shipment. Your reward is waiting in the terminal. They've also asked if there is anything they can do for you.
Dialogue.87006D444141563D514518AA582D2D62_A_E_Moo: They can pay us more and demand less.
Dialogue.87006D444141563D514518AA582D2D62_A_M_Moo: They could give us our rewards faster.
Dialogue.87006D444141563D514518AA582D2D62_A_S_Moo: No, we have everything we need.
Dialogue.AAE8F83545496755DD3D26A3EA26A9B6_A_G_E_M: Unfortunately, the contract we have with them does not allow for negotiations of this kind. One of the benefits they do offer is a pollution report on Arcadia-7.
Dialogue.AAE8F83545496755DD3D26A3EA26A9B6_A_G_S_M: Great. The Moon Energy Corporation can send you spectroscopy reports on Arcadia-7 so that you can see the planet's pollution levels, those should ease your mind.
Dialogue.70D1AB45489CCC87BB6A9C948CC16893_A_P_Moo: Oh that doesn't matter. Information like that is useless at the moment.
Dialogue.0D3C276145CE8BEA6C5D828C7337E77D_A_G_Moo: Sent! The Moon Energy Corporation is very pleased with your services. More rewards await you in the terminal.
Dialogue.A753604F4152F95B7624978F5DF3B113_A_G_Moo: Wonderful! The Moon Energy Corporation thanks you for your shipment. They also want to take this opportunity to let you know that no inhabitant of the Balkan region was harmed while the Wind Turbine technology was being developed.
Dialogue.857F468B44841EF9AC227BBEF985165A_A_M_Moo: That's a strange thing to say.
Dialogue.4ACDFB4540567B73A86A2A8CED8FC113_A_G_Moo: I am not authorized to continue speaking on this subject.
Dialogue.0BEE8AEA43AC53BDC13A9E99C67679C9_A_G_Moo: Excellent! The Moon Energy Corporation remains very impressed with your services! Rewards are waiting in the terminal.
Dialogue.172455E34E352207415FFA81508AD511_A_G_Moo: Bravo! The Moon Energy Corporation thanks you for another shipment. It also reminds you that if you were to meet someone spreading false information as to the conditions existing in the colonies on Arcadia-7 you are required to report that person to a designated representative of the company.
Dialogue.C1DE92DC455A4635F4EDB2A07FA339DA_A_E_Moo: If I meet someone here who's alive besides us then I'll be too busy jumping with joy to report them.
Dialogue.C1DE92DC455A4635F4EDB2A07FA339DA_A_M_Moo: Even if by some miracle I were to see someone else, I'd never rat them out.
Dialogue.C1DE92DC455A4635F4EDB2A07FA339DA_A_P_Moo: The probability of seeing someone else alive here besides us four is too low to be taken seriously.
Dialogue.C1DE92DC455A4635F4EDB2A07FA339DA_A_S_Moo: The people we meet here aren't very talkative.
Dialogue.77E0842F4903471038AC58BBAC4D72CC_A_G_Moo: The Moon Energy Corporation thanks you for your cooperation.
Dialogue.B5C4891147F9BF82FCB4E6962AF24337_A_G_Moo: Great work. The Moon Energy Corporation thanks you for the shipment and wishes you happy holidays.
Dialogue.6E8895734B9E9BE4D93589A50EF5A7F7_A_E_Moo: Cheesecrackers, it's Christmas on Earth already?
Dialogue.6E8895734B9E9BE4D93589A50EF5A7F7_A_M_Moo: I didn't know it was Christmas. What's the date exactly back on Earth?
Dialogue.6E8895734B9E9BE4D93589A50EF5A7F7_A_P_Moo: Oh, my sense of time must be warped because Arcadia's revolutions are not in sync with its orbit around Ruptura. It's Christmas back on Earth? That means it's December, right?
Dialogue.6E8895734B9E9BE4D93589A50EF5A7F7_A_S_Moo: Time flows differently here. Is it Christmas back on Earth?
Dialogue.D872381E4C243A77554CA4899C3F5605_A_G_Moo: I'm sorry, I'm not authorized to disclose classified information. But I can tell you there are presents waiting in the terminal. Does it matter what the occasion is?
Dialogue.D52F17494891BD371DB141B4B3051FC3_A_G_Moo: The shipment has reached its destination. The Moon Energy Corporation would also like to point out the efficiency of the generators you are using. Did you know that the Solar Generator on the surface of Arcadia is up to 18 times more efficient than the generator made by the company Sunny Home used in smaller colonies on Mars?
Dialogue.3350287E4129425146C8A2A3DC7AA281_A_E_Moo: No way? Photovoltaic cells work better when they're closer to the star?
Dialogue.3350287E4129425146C8A2A3DC7AA281_A_M_Moo: Moon Energy controls 90% of the energy market and they still need to spread propaganda against other companies.
Dialogue.3350287E4129425146C8A2A3DC7AA281_A_P_Moo: Of course they are. The levels of sunlight are much higher here. The fact that they're only 18 times better is curious. I would need to run the numbers but it might mean that Sunny Home's cells could be more efficient.
Dialogue.3350287E4129425146C8A2A3DC7AA281_A_S_Moo: This isn't my specialty, but isn't that because there's way more sunlight on Arcadia?
Dialogue.F440FD2341017099477FAEB06E331681_A_G_P_M: You don’t need to run anything!
Dialogue.F440FD2341017099477FAEB06E331681_A_G_S_M: There's no way to check. Moon Energy is the sole provider of energy for Arcadia-7.
Dialogue.656E1FBA462DD173165CFF9DF37FE3F5_A_G_Moo: Congratulations! The Moon Energy Corporation thanks you for the shipment!
Dialogue.CFA33FA4442B9E39452A5BB65AAB276E_A_G_Moo: Good job! The Moon Energy Corporation has received another shipment. They are truly grateful. At this point you must have noticed how reliable their equipment is. They would like to offer you a discount on a generator when you get back to the Solar System.
Dialogue.AF0E11134558344EDB53DCA6AF46A395_A_E_Moo: I don't know if I'll be able to afford my own generator, but I always love a good deal. How much is the discount?
Dialogue.AF0E11134558344EDB53DCA6AF46A395_A_M_Moo: I need to use their energy back home anyway, maybe my own generator will lower the cost. How much is the discount?
Dialogue.AF0E11134558344EDB53DCA6AF46A395_A_P_Moo: Excellent! They really do make great stuff. How big is the discount?
Dialogue.AF0E11134558344EDB53DCA6AF46A395_A_S_Moo: I have to admit they really are reliable. Even looking at what remains of the previous expeditions, the generators are still in good shape. What's the discount?
Dialogue.5C6EBC224BD07FC35F36ED97220747DA_A_G_Moo: It's exactly 0%! Oh, wait, I got that mixed up with the amount of carbon dioxide released into the atmosphere by Moon Energy generators.
Dialogue.9BCBB1574F3BFB39601CD1932C0E79B4_A_E_Moo: The generators don't release carbon dioxide, but their production is a different matter.
Dialogue.9BCBB1574F3BFB39601CD1932C0E79B4_A_M_Moo: Wonderful news. Let's see the climate data for their factories too. Or the medical records of their employees. And what about that report from the LessSleeves organization where…
Dialogue.9BCBB1574F3BFB39601CD1932C0E79B4_A_P_Moo: The energy created by the generators is neutral to the climate, but the things they make them out of…
Dialogue.9BCBB1574F3BFB39601CD1932C0E79B4_A_S_Moo: Of course. Generators by themselves don't create carbon dioxide. So what's the discount?
Dialogue.B385A23944982810183862997DA1696C_A_G_Moo: The Moon Energy Corporation thanks you for another shipment. They would also like to congratulate you. As members of the Moon family you too have received the prestigious National Fair Trade Green Energy Peace Award!
Dialogue.8C1FEF15493CC93F2F22CF9BFAECD38E_A_E_Moo: I'm not surprised since they don't pollute the environment and they didn't cause any harm in the Balkans…
Dialogue.8C1FEF15493CC93F2F22CF9BFAECD38E_A_M_Moo: Isn't that award sponsored by the Moon Energy Corporation?
Dialogue.8C1FEF15493CC93F2F22CF9BFAECD38E_A_P_Moo: Another award to add to my collection!
Dialogue.8C1FEF15493CC93F2F22CF9BFAECD38E_A_S_Moo: Is that going to help us in any way on our mission?
Dialogue.37E5F6D44A2295AE0501D8843E5ED0C9_A_M_Not: Life would not exist without water.
Dialogue.37E5F6D44A2295AE0501D8843E5ED0C9_A_P_Not: Two liters of water a day is the minimum.
Dialogue.5DD556DF44DE519866BBBC975CC6ABCF_A_E_Pic: I think I can use this.
Dialogue.5DD556DF44DE519866BBBC975CC6ABCF_A_M_Pic: I think I can use this.
Dialogue.5DD556DF44DE519866BBBC975CC6ABCF_A_P_Pic: I think I can use this.
Dialogue.5DD556DF44DE519866BBBC975CC6ABCF_A_S_Pic: I think I can use this.
Dialogue.85E985774588CFEA486BCABF0DD63B43_A_P_Pla: Lunch is over. Let's get back to work.
Dialogue.F1E8BED34FFE451A252215B1EC8278FD_A_P_Pos: I have to check my results.
Dialogue.BFAC8DCA45DF1C8B0A2E6B94309F4EC8_A_M_Pos: May I help you with something?
Dialogue.D662D7EA44755587D8B50A8E5FEA6890_A_E_Pos: First step: Don't die. Second step: Repeat.
Dialogue.9C3FADAF42FBB240CF3493B09C410651_A_P_Res: I died? What a waste of time!
Dialogue.E5DAB2E9483D6FC14CA7D2A79AC88BE0_A_M_Res: My head is spinning a bit.
Dialogue.E5DAB2E9483D6FC14CA7D2A79AC88BE0_A_P_Res: It's time to get back to work!
Dialogue.BED5C6D045424FB38CBA8B9E9C83F296_A_M_Res: If only everyone could use this technology.
Dialogue.BED5C6D045424FB38CBA8B9E9C83F296_A_S_Res: Dying is easy. Living is harder.
Dialogue.C8267D1240E59EAE790AA6AEB1154BF7_A_G_SWE: Ruptura's eruption has started. Prepare for impact.
Dialogue.25E7F2AF4EB7C7703AA111BCC89F4AD7_A_G_SWE: Ruptura's core is unstable. Head to safety immediately.
Dialogue.3B84A6F2484570A74F7EA28482AC1EE6_A_G_SWF: Temperature is going back to normal.
Dialogue.8D47C0704A3DB7A57C91C5AD982B8F99_A_G_SWF: Temperature has decreased from critical levels.
Dialogue.D0B91330468FA964236731A2F4D07E01_A_G_SWF: Warning! The planet is being incinerated.
Dialogue.437A2C88444A2A428BA7958DC0717A2E_A_G_SWF: I'm detecting increased Ruptura activity. Prepare for a wave.
Dialogue.4E67B8FD4E12B02D823016908DD843AC_A_G_SWF: Ruptura activity detected. I recommend finding a safe place.
Dialogue.F3EA44EA466B0E362939D1B429AE0E88_A_G_SWR: The rupture is in its stable stage. The climate of Arcadia is returning to normal.
Dialogue.C3E2EF8D4CAA057A960A278E40D9BE91_A_G_SWR: Ruptura status: stable. Arcadia status: stable.
Dialogue.23A95CF9483CDE9290ED0D9B28AC38D3_A_G_Sel: Excellent work! The Selenian Corporation thanks you for the shipment. Your rewards are waiting in the Corporate Terminal.
Dialogue.CA1670974B6F1133306C26BCD5585AC6_A_G_Sel: Your cargo has reached the Selenian Corporation! You've completed another order and your reward is waiting in the Corporate Terminal.
Dialogue.B718F80D4F8B46222B1D76A13450579C_A_G_Sel: Selenian has received the products it ordered! They're very pleased, you could become the best crew they've ever worked with.
Dialogue.7D1063B4438CFBCFA16EDD925612C304_A_G_Sel: Good Work! Selenian thanks you for the shipment. They're very impressed. The other crews they had previously worked with weren't even half as good!
Dialogue.93260D7A4BE5F6272493629C62E2D0BB_A_E_Sel: That's what I'm talking about! Are we gonna get extra compensation for this?
Dialogue.93260D7A4BE5F6272493629C62E2D0BB_A_M_Sel: Since they're so happy with our work can we count on additional benefits?
Dialogue.93260D7A4BE5F6272493629C62E2D0BB_A_P_Sel: Of course we're the best, the qualifications of most of the people sent here are staggering. I assume that the rewards granted to us will reflect the quality of our work?
Dialogue.93260D7A4BE5F6272493629C62E2D0BB_A_S_Sel: Does that come with any additional benefits?
Dialogue.5F0051414AF364E32B6E1CA4443F3BC1_A_G_Sel: Not that I'm aware of. You're simply doing what's expected of you according to the contract, the other crews were not even doing that.
Dialogue.A71839034A74E297070780A29E56A850_A_G_Sel: Congratulations! Selenian received its order! Your reward, as always, is waiting in the Corporate Terminal.
Dialogue.07E0626148B26D6A516CDBABABA445DC_A_G_Sel: The cargo reached its destination. Selenian thanks you for the order, your work is restoring their faith in the prison system.
Dialogue.24117C774BBBD9BF53FA7A8635C70C9F_A_E_Sel: I don't know if I wanted to restore their faith in that corrupt system but it's good they're happy with our work.
Dialogue.24117C774BBBD9BF53FA7A8635C70C9F_A_M_Sel: The prison system is the main tool of the criminal regime. I don't want to hear comments like that.
Dialogue.24117C774BBBD9BF53FA7A8635C70C9F_A_P_Sel: What do you mean restoring? Using socially maladjusted individuals for labor is the only reasonable solution. How could they doubt it?
Dialogue.24117C774BBBD9BF53FA7A8635C70C9F_A_S_Sel: The prison system always worked, it's just a matter of proper motivation and leadership.
Dialogue.8CDD436F43545ABB2FCB9090AC741B1B_A_G_E_S: Always look on the bright side of life.
Dialogue.8CDD436F43545ABB2FCB9090AC741B1B_A_G_M_S: But they just praised you! Don't be so dramatic, you won't change galactic law from Arcadia. Take the compliment.
Dialogue.8CDD436F43545ABB2FCB9090AC741B1B_A_G_P_S: Considering their experiences with previous expeditions I'm not surprised they doubted it.
Dialogue.8CDD436F43545ABB2FCB9090AC741B1B_A_G_S_S: And you're clearly a great leader!
Dialogue.550F495B44998BADE2F910A990D6DF05_A_G_Sel: Good work! The shipment to Selenian has been sent! They didn't expect such efficiency. Especially after the previous crew from the Orpheus VII mission.
Dialogue.0AE675F949877184FC9489A63391E727_A_G_Sel: They've been dubbed the most incompetent crew in the history of Arcadia-7's exploration. They rebelled and demanded that fresh fruit and vegetables be sent to them from Earth. Selenian couldn't let that happen, the costs were enormous.
Dialogue.8B05490F44BD49ECD94F4CA6C29F386D_A_E_Sel: That's it? Just because they wanted to eat some carrots they're the worst crew in history?
Dialogue.8B05490F44BD49ECD94F4CA6C29F386D_A_M_Sel: They wanted to be treated humanely and that made them the worst crew in history? Quite an overreaction.
Dialogue.8B05490F44BD49ECD94F4CA6C29F386D_A_P_Sel: Idiots. Arcadia-7 is full of delicious food. They should've focused on their job rather than worry about their cravings.
Dialogue.8B05490F44BD49ECD94F4CA6C29F386D_A_S_Sel: That's understandable. Sending cargo like that to a planet full of edible plants is a waste.
Dialogue.79ED80824FA1B7EDBEF1EAAD42523C23_A_G_E_S: The crew refused to perform their duties. The whole crew was dead within a week.
Dialogue.79ED80824FA1B7EDBEF1EAAD42523C23_A_G_M_S: The crew refused to perform their duties. The whole crew was dead within a week.
Dialogue.79ED80824FA1B7EDBEF1EAAD42523C23_A_G_P_S: That's exactly what Selenian believed but the crew refused to perform their duties. After a week, every crew member was dead.
Dialogue.79ED80824FA1B7EDBEF1EAAD42523C23_A_G_S_S: That's exactly what Selenian believed but the crew refused to perform their duties. After a week, every crew member was dead.
Dialogue.99E600514048EADB3D45A9B22AD1F29F_A_G_Sel: While refusing to carry out their responsibilities they also neglected to properly protect their base. Ruptura and the Vermin don't care if you don't like the food. One needs to remain humble on Arcadia-7.
Dialogue.404081C54DDE0E5D50C43F8025B05792_A_G_Sel: Superb! Selenian thanks you for another shipment and sends your rewards. This also sets a new record. You've lasted the longest out of any crew without filing a complaint.
Dialogue.51C4B8EF4414DF8C9B698097692111E2_A_G_Sel: Of course not. Mr. Claywood wants to remain on good terms with the Selenian Corporation so that option was removed from the contract.
Dialogue.9DD136EB4B2F0DCE12D3C986CF35F94A_A_G_Sel: Wonderful! Selenian thanks you for the shipment! You've been named Convict of the Month! Upon your return to Earth you will receive a certificate and a commemorative mug!
Dialogue.1D1BD6AA426A66FA05107BAE3B484FBD_A_M_Sel: Convict of the Month. How insulting.
Dialogue.1D1BD6AA426A66FA05107BAE3B484FBD_A_P_Sel: I don't care about the certificate. But a mug's a mug.
Dialogue.3B764C644D389CA03FF8E0AD9C940E80_A_G_Sel: You're doing great. Selenian received its cargo. In addition to your reward, I have good news. They're so happy with your work compared to previous crews that they're offering you a job after your mission on Arcadia-7 is complete.
Dialogue.45048ABA4B74CE1CBA8FA7B032F6F38B_A_G_Sel: Essentially the same job you're doing now but exclusively for Selenian.
Dialogue.FF6EEC904E65E0B1F77368925BA98277_A_E_Sel: You've gotta be kidding. I plan to open a workshop when I get back and be my own boss.
Dialogue.FF6EEC904E65E0B1F77368925BA98277_A_M_Sel: I plan to return to treating people back on Earth.
Dialogue.FF6EEC904E65E0B1F77368925BA98277_A_P_Sel: No way. I'm going to have a lot of research to do at the university.
Dialogue.FF6EEC904E65E0B1F77368925BA98277_A_S_Sel: That part of my life will be over by then.
Dialogue.0CF7AE284A58743DEAB04186DBBBBCD3_A_G_Sel: I'll let them know you'll consider it!
Dialogue.32E5F7F1453FDDB187DB44BFFFB7AEED_A_G_Sel: Incredible work! The Selenian Corporation has received your shipment and with it you've surpassed the second best factory on Arcadia-7 in terms of the amount of cargo delivered!
Dialogue.05B2C61448079E2C67065AB2B4A366FB_A_E_Sel: Holy crab, we really are good at this. Selenian had a lot of factories and we still delivered the most products.
Dialogue.05B2C61448079E2C67065AB2B4A366FB_A_M_Sel: That's good news. That means we have a realistic chance of paying off our debt and freeing ourselves.
Dialogue.05B2C61448079E2C67065AB2B4A366FB_A_P_Sel: Incredible. Looking at the number of bases set up by Selenian, some of them had to be very efficient, statistically speaking.
Dialogue.05B2C61448079E2C67065AB2B4A366FB_A_S_Sel: Hmm, that is pretty good. Especially since Selenian had a lot of factories.
Dialogue.B44C2332495AAEC03D86838024307815_A_G_Sel: The Selenian Corporation is the most expansive among the companies you work with. Despite having the largest number of bases set up on Arcadia-7 nowhere did they find anyone as competent as you!
Dialogue.18DE836E4C000B098378CB8BD63D74B5_A_E_Sel: This is starting to sound fishy. We're not THAT good.
Dialogue.18DE836E4C000B098378CB8BD63D74B5_A_M_Sel: That's impossible. Everyone ever sent here was the best in their field.
Dialogue.18DE836E4C000B098378CB8BD63D74B5_A_P_Sel: Naturally. Imagine how a good a crew we'd have if there was four of me here.
Dialogue.18DE836E4C000B098378CB8BD63D74B5_A_S_Sel: That's improbable. Are they sucking up to us?
Dialogue.7CEC5D9246438D3E5BCF71BD65F4F8B6_A_G_Sel: Most of the bases built here in the past few years have also received this distinction. It appears the Selenian Corporation draws its conclusions and each new crew is simply better than the last one!
Dialogue.EB42F1154D270E434BFDA487E7A0D97D_A_E_Tel: I'm never gonna get used to this.
Dialogue.EB42F1154D270E434BFDA487E7A0D97D_A_P_Tel: It's a weird feeling but it's worth it.
Dialogue.5F866B63484EAB1D06536D9D23C54B54_A_M_Tel: We don't know what effect frequent teleportation can have on the mind.
Dialogue.5F866B63484EAB1D06536D9D23C54B54_A_P_Tel: This technology never ceases to amaze me.
Dialogue.9E56640B4F7375178344378978AB88D9_A_E_Tel: That was a little better this time.
Dialogue.9E56640B4F7375178344378978AB88D9_A_P_Tel: The severity of symptoms does not decrease after subsequent teleportations. <slightly disappointed>
Dialogue.9E56640B4F7375178344378978AB88D9_A_S_Tel: Teleportation successful with no side effects.
Dialogue.986FD9944BDE610C00D8448C2C8C9BD4_A_M_Tel: I feel better than the first time.
Dialogue.986FD9944BDE610C00D8448C2C8C9BD4_A_P_Tel: Feeling ill is a small price to pay for progress.
Dialogue.B2E467A742D4EEDC5D681BB254C88494_A_S_Thi: If I don't drink something soon I'm gonna die.
Dialogue.8A53E5A747D4CA5D670462A3C1CB1138_A_P_Thi: I'm so thirsty my head hurts.
Dialogue.0C169C1848779D131CAE4992F80A93AE_A_M_Tox: Ugh... Symptoms indicate the presence of toxins.
Dialogue.0C169C1848779D131CAE4992F80A93AE_A_P_Tox: <groans> The human digestive system is too delicate.
Dialogue.2D6E73954EA2EF0393FE79968D8B1639_A_G_E_T: Life vitals normal. Prisoner E4101, welcome to the Argos program. Your adventure with the Claywood Corporation begins right now!
Dialogue.2D6E73954EA2EF0393FE79968D8B1639_A_G_M_T: Life vitals normal. Prisoner B1690, welcome to the Argos program. Your adventure with the Claywood Corporation begins right now!
Dialogue.2D6E73954EA2EF0393FE79968D8B1639_A_G_P_T: Life vitals normal. Prisoner P0212, welcome to the Argos program. Your adventure with the Claywood Corporation begins right now!
Dialogue.2D6E73954EA2EF0393FE79968D8B1639_A_G_S_T: Life vitals normal. Prisoner S8466, welcome to the Argos program. Your adventure with the Claywood Corporation begins right now!
Dialogue.7D71CA5B4139153A0CE00FA28400BC82_A_G_Tut: Great work as usual. Now build the Analyzer and research some local flora with it.
Dialogue.996FC1CD4F88E123FD0A5C9D19DA244D_A_G_Tut: We've just unlocked new building schematics for you. Can you guess what they're for?
Dialogue.E16C211F4A4FA8A1279408B4E02EC83E_A_E_Tut: I used these machines on Mars. The rails are for drones that will carry resources between buildings. As for the Ore Excavator, I refuse to say what it does. I have many years of mining experience.
Dialogue.E16C211F4A4FA8A1279408B4E02EC83E_A_M_Tut: Let's not play these games, you'll tell me anyway.
Dialogue.E16C211F4A4FA8A1279408B4E02EC83E_A_P_Tut: A trivial question. Of course I know what they're for. We'll automate production by excavating deposits and sending them between buildings using rails.
Dialogue.E16C211F4A4FA8A1279408B4E02EC83E_A_S_Tut: I assume they are industrial machines making the mission easier somehow.
Dialogue.8526CEA94326DACB711F80B72A15702F_A_G_E_T: Lack of knowledge is nothing to be embarrassed about. The Ore Excavator excavates ores.
Dialogue.8526CEA94326DACB711F80B72A15702F_A_G_M_T: Maybe at least give it a try? I'll be sad if you don't even try.
Dialogue.8526CEA94326DACB711F80B72A15702F_A_G_P_T: Impressive! You've used equipment like this before?
Dialogue.8526CEA94326DACB711F80B72A15702F_A_G_S_T: And how would they do that?
Dialogue.4281B84843C31E6D91C4D9BD485C1028_A_E_Tut: You don't say! That explains everything!
Dialogue.4281B84843C31E6D91C4D9BD485C1028_A_M_Tut: <sigh> We have an excavating machine and some transport system for cargo. I guess it's to automate the excavation process?
Dialogue.4281B84843C31E6D91C4D9BD485C1028_A_P_Tut: Hardly! It just doesn't make logical sense to extract everything by hand and run around from building to building. You'd waste my potential if I had to do that.
Dialogue.4281B84843C31E6D91C4D9BD485C1028_A_S_Tut: In any way you decide, you're the one giving orders here. I assume I'll find out in a second.
Dialogue.3B0257834BDDE6367CB0DE8EE93FC5BC_A_G_M_T: Good answer, but please smile next time!
Dialogue.3B0257834BDDE6367CB0DE8EE93FC5BC_A_G_P_T: Exactly! Let's take advantage of those three doctorates!
Dialogue.DDDCDC5E48B3C8A78C2038A19F33BD7B_A_G_Tut: The heart of the meteorite is very valuable, you can use it to create your Base Core. It will allow you to build other structures and will protect them from the lethal influence of Ruptura. Trust me, you'll want to be protected.
Dialogue.14F3DFC74DC92DC674C4C5B664DBDBD9_A_G_Tut: As long as you follow our instructions you'll have nothing to worry about.
As long as you follow our instructions you'll have nothing to worry about.
Dialogue.9CCF779B4069C1FDAA71B99BA311E002_A_G_Tut: Please don't move. I want to run a holistic scan.
Dialogue.B9D03E734F639FF07FA8CE88C8F2DC6B_A_G_Tut: Great! Now build a Corporate Terminal. That will allow you to complete assignments for different companies which will in turn give you access to new buildings!
Dialogue.9EB4040A415C2BAE2F4F6CB90C2DA35B_A_G_Tut: Arcadia is often bombarded by meteorites which are rich in resources. You have been equipped with a tool to acquire them. Use it to extract what's most valuable in the meteorite.
Dialogue.A4852D3F48FB3E26B3CF969343843395_A_G_Tut: Good work! You'll need building materials to build the rest of the base. You can create them with the printer in your lander. But gather the necessary components first. Use the Harvester to extract them, just like you did with the meteorite.
Dialogue.68B651B245E86AB28C8395ACDD185154_A_G_Tut: Once you research enough plants, send the data to our scientists and claim your reward. In the future, you will need to decide which corporations you want to share your research with. The data from Arcadia is so valuable that companies prefer to keep it to themselves and will appreciate it when you choose them.
Dialogue.BD313E5644848FAA32FF62AC4CFD0F89_A_G_Tut: Great job! This is the end of your introductory training! But remember that Arcadia-7 is a dangerous place and a person will spend their entire life, or lives rather, learning from it. Stay alert, gather information and don't worry, I'm always by your side watching your every move.
Dialogue.6B424D734EA394DC7A6258B79C0D9C8F_A_G_Tut: It's for your own safety! I will now remove the introductory training restrictions. Location barrier: disabled. Sedative injector: disconnected. Communications channel: active. Awakening other crew members: ready.
Dialogue.9756EF734FD868A9472E2CA0DAC1D9E5_A_G_Tut: The Claywood Corporation hopes you have a wonderful adventure and quickly pay off your debt! Good luck!
Dialogue.921BD5E241C45C03DBC43EB1780C5AD9_A_G_Tut: Everything's ready! Now build the habitat that will protect your sleeve from Arcadia's dangers. Remember that your body is also a Claywood Corporate investment so it would be good to create a comfortable place for it.
Dialogue.AEA2756D46F95534769F5D830D00A838_A_G_Tut: Hello! I am GAL - your Galactic Assistance Liaison. The Claywood Corporation would like to apologize for any inconvenience you may have experienced. You can now exit the lander and begin your introductory training.
Dialogue.55DA09824ED77C78BF36B5A61DD890F8_A_E_Tut: Right away? No breakfast or coffee? You're not much different from the colony overseers.
Dialogue.55DA09824ED77C78BF36B5A61DD890F8_A_M_Tut: Hello. Training is a good sign—in the mines, they had us start working right away.
Dialogue.55DA09824ED77C78BF36B5A61DD890F8_A_P_Tut: I'm finally here. Let's get this training over with—I want to get to work.
Dialogue.4B88029D415B2D53C01F2E8154F24231_A_G_Tut: As soon as we get the package your reputation will increase which will unlock new schematics for you.
Dialogue.E6D50A0D4064FFAA3649ED8224BD4673_A_G_Tut: The first reward was free, but you'll have to work for the next one. Send us some titanium.
Dialogue.8AB1944041BFFF96258CB0BF3DFC121C_A_E_Tut: How am I supposed to send what I've gathered back to Earth?
Dialogue.8AB1944041BFFF96258CB0BF3DFC121C_A_M_Tut: How am I supposed to send what I've gathered back to Earth?
Dialogue.8AB1944041BFFF96258CB0BF3DFC121C_A_P_Tut: How am I supposed to send what I've gathered back to Earth?
Dialogue.8AB1944041BFFF96258CB0BF3DFC121C_A_S_Tut: How am I supposed to send what I've gathered back to Earth?
Dialogue.C9FDD2BB4BC6CDEC4E61FFB503E44290_A_G_Tut: The same way you got here, but in reverse. Look up at the sky. Once you build an Orbital Cargo Launcher, it will send supplies right through that Rift. It will cover lightyears in seconds!
Dialogue.4C60450A4AC66E1FCEEFD69D947FF571_A_G_Tut: It's time for the final stage of introductory training. Raw materials aren't very useful to corporations, since they need to produce something with them anyway. Use the buildings you have available and automate the production of the more valuable items.
Dialogue.4189441A42FDD112554D12A5DE66BF91_A_E_Tut: Why can't they process them themselves? They have factories across the entire solar system.
Dialogue.4189441A42FDD112554D12A5DE66BF91_A_M_Tut: Why can't they process them themselves? They have factories across the entire solar system.
Dialogue.4189441A42FDD112554D12A5DE66BF91_A_S_Tut: Why can't they process them themselves? They have factories across the entire solar system.
Dialogue.A8C0285A47A307DA8AEF9E960954AAC6_A_G_Tut: This will be best explained by a private conversation recorded between two executives at the Griffits Military Corporation.
Dialogue.17970E03462C2DB52907E3B635DFD84D_A_HW_Tu: So, you're telling me all of the tax laws apply only to the solar system?
Dialogue.262735944AE92F38A4E51BB95B5F77C8_A_SA_Tu: Bro, the mining tax, the cosmic fees, deductions from extraterrestrial income, the cost of insuring sensitive cargo. Legally none of that applies to us. They can't even hit us with tariffs. It's free money, man!
Dialogue.3234171A43362DD8B14F07A4A0279995_A_E_Tut: I don't know why I asked.
Dialogue.3234171A43362DD8B14F07A4A0279995_A_M_Tut: I don't know why I asked.
Dialogue.3234171A43362DD8B14F07A4A0279995_A_P_Tut: I don't know why I asked.
Dialogue.3234171A43362DD8B14F07A4A0279995_A_S_Tut: I don't know why I asked.
Dialogue.4284EA4149882C859D43ED949670E283_A_G_Tut: Now that you have your shelter build a printer inside it. That way you will always have it nearby thus optimizing your work.
Dialogue.7A22742142C565EB772C1A82BBA3EFA0_A_G_Tut: Now that the raw materials are being extracted automatically you'll have more time to build out your base.
Dialogue.D7572E9E4FB486DC4034959A24891672_A_E_Tut: I have a question. Why didn't you install all available building schematics for me from the start? That would speed up my work even more.
Dialogue.D7572E9E4FB486DC4034959A24891672_A_M_Tut: I have a question. Why didn't you install all available building schematics for me from the start? That would speed up my work even more.
Dialogue.D7572E9E4FB486DC4034959A24891672_A_P_Tut: I have a question. Why didn't you install all available building schematics for me from the start? That would speed up my work even more.
Dialogue.D7572E9E4FB486DC4034959A24891672_A_S_Tut: I have a question. Why didn't you install all available building schematics for me from the start? That would speed up my work even more.
Dialogue.B02E14554E388EB559606DBC70CEBFB7_A_G_Tut: All of the machines made available to you during your mission are delicate and extremely expensive. They are also bound by NDAs and patents.
Dialogue.FD28903F47D0AA414158DDA38C96758B_A_E_Tut: But I already signed the NDA.
Dialogue.FD28903F47D0AA414158DDA38C96758B_A_M_Tut: But I already signed the NDA.
Dialogue.FD28903F47D0AA414158DDA38C96758B_A_P_Tut: But I already signed the NDA.
Dialogue.FD28903F47D0AA414158DDA38C96758B_A_S_Tut: But I already signed the NDA.
Dialogue.8520D02941180A290C50C192FFBE60AA_A_G_Tut: None of the companies working with the Claywood Corporation have granted permission to give you everything right away. You need to prove you are worthy of using the more advanced equipment.
Dialogue.41E52B264338F564B49AD98E88270289_A_G_Tut: This will be best explained by the words of Annika Fisher, the CEO of Future Health Solutions, one of our partners. Playing recording.
Dialogue.2DE18D9943E168C1BD1368A1C1722062_A_AF_Tu: There's no way I'm giving those degenerates my patents. They don't care about the law or intellectual property. But if it becomes necessary and they actually deserve it then so be it. Don't quote me on that.
Dialogue.715DA88D4C7EF83FED66CEB5A190081B_A_E_Tut: I gotta admit, working here seems a lot better than at the penal colony. We definitely have better equipment.
Dialogue.715DA88D4C7EF83FED66CEB5A190081B_A_M_Tut: I wonder what the catch is.
Dialogue.715DA88D4C7EF83FED66CEB5A190081B_A_P_Tut: I can't believe I'm here. Everything here is fascinating.
Dialogue.0F1943EC40EF65A3CBEB819471E4C7AF_A_G_E_T: The Claywood Corporation spares no expense to ensure its workers have access to the best possible equipment.
Dialogue.0F1943EC40EF65A3CBEB819471E4C7AF_A_G_M_T: I have no idea what you mean.
Dialogue.0F1943EC40EF65A3CBEB819471E4C7AF_A_G_P_T: The Claywood Corporation is very glad to see your enthusiasm. Most convicts do not share it.
Dialogue.0F1943EC40EF65A3CBEB819471E4C7AF_A_G_S_T: Of course, as your assistant I will answer all of your questions.
Dialogue.FD27595C4BF0ED148BF48FBACE42E98A_A_E_Tut: The view isn't bad either. I got used to seeing only gray rocks against a dark sky.
Dialogue.FD27595C4BF0ED148BF48FBACE42E98A_A_M_Tut: You brought me here for this relatively peaceful job. You gave me the best possible equipment. It's nice and calm here, like it was on Earth when I was a kid. But I know the stories about Arcadia, I know that nearly everyone who was here before me had died. So I ask again, what's the catch?
Dialogue.FD27595C4BF0ED148BF48FBACE42E98A_A_P_Tut: Most of them are usually idiots who are unable to see the potential in being a pioneer on a new world.
Dialogue.FD27595C4BF0ED148BF48FBACE42E98A_A_S_Tut: Why did Claywood send someone with military experience to mine minerals?
